```tsx
  test("the decisions: a measure in force, one a later decision lifted, one that ended with the case's decision, a seal that ended with the admin's answer, and beside a field reset that it was written once", () => {
    const LIFTING = "0f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-5a4b3c2d1e0f";
    const action = (id: string, kind: CaseView["decisions"][number]["actions"][number]["kind"], more: Partial<CaseView["decisions"][number]["actions"][number]> = {}) => ({ id, kind, mediaId: null, noEffect: null, inForce: false, reversesActionId: null, liftedBy: null, sealed: null, ...more });
    const WITHHOLD = "1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d";
    const out = page(
      accountCase({
        decisions: [
          decision({
            actions: [
              action(WITHHOLD, "withhold", { liftedBy: LIFTING }),
              action("2b3c4d5e-6f7a-4b8c-9d0e-1f2a3b4c5d6e", "withhold_media", { mediaId: IMAGE_ONE }),
              action("3c4d5e6f-7a8b-4c9d-ae1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f", "seal_media", { sealed: { posts: 1, images: 2, deletedPosts: 0, list: [] } }),
              action("4d5e6f7a-8b9c-4dae-bf2a-3b4c5d6e7f8a", "reset_display_name", { inForce: true }),
              action("5e6f7a8b-9cad-4ebf-803b-4c5d6e7f8a9b", "reset_bio", { noEffect: "already" }),
            ],
          }),
          decision({ id: LIFTING, kind: "correction", outcome: "reversed", decidedAt: "2026-10-01T10:15:00.000Z", actions: [action("6f7a8b9c-adbe-4fc0-914c-5d6e7f8a9bac", "restore", { reversesActionId: WITHHOLD })] }),
        ],
      }),
    );
    // What lifted a measure: the decision that reversed it, by its time.
    expect(out).toContain("<li>Withhold the post: lifted by the decision of 2026-10-01 10:15</li>");
    expect(out).toContain(`<li>Withhold one image <code>${IMAGE_ONE}</code>: ended with the case&#x27;s decision</li>`);
    expect(out).toContain("Seal the images this case reaches: ended with the admin&#x27;s answer");
    expect(out).toContain("<li>Reset display name: in force; written once; the field as it reads now is shown above</li>");
    expect(out).toContain("<li>Reset bio: ended with the case&#x27;s decision; changed nothing when imposed; written once; the field as it reads now is shown above</li>");
    // A reversal is no measure: it has no state of its own.
    expect(out).toContain("<li>Lift the restriction of the post</li>");
    // Each decision's kind and outcome in the console's own words, one table each.
    expect(out).toContain(`<strong>${DECISION_KINDS.interim}</strong>: ${DECISION_OUTCOMES.restricted}, 2026-10-01 09:00, by `);
    expect(out).toContain(`<strong>${DECISION_KINDS.correction}</strong>: ${DECISION_OUTCOMES.reversed}, 2026-10-01 10:15, by `);
    expect(DECISION_KINDS).toEqual({ interim: "While deciding", final: "Final decision", review: "Review of an appeal", correction: "Correction" });
    // An item's outcome, once answered.
    expect(page(postCase({ items: [item({ outcome: "restricted_rule", answeredBy: LIFTING })] }))).toContain(`<p>Answered: ${OUTCOME_WORDS.restricted_rule}.</p>`);
    expect(OUTCOME_WORDS.not_available).toBe("nothing live at the link");
  });

  test("a fresh snapshot is offered when the target differs from the newest one or that one is withheld, and a withheld snapshot shows no content", () => {
    expect(targetDiffers(postCase())).toBe(false);
    expect(targetDiffers(postCase({ target: { ...postCase().target, type: "post", state: "deleted_by_author" } as CaseView["target"] }))).toBe(true);
    const withheld = postCase({ snapshots: [{ id: "8c9daebf-c0d1-42e3-845f-7a8b9cadbecf", takenAt: "2026-10-01T08:00:00.000Z", digest: "ab".repeat(32), withheld: true }] });
    expect(targetDiffers(withheld)).toBe(true);
    const out = page(withheld);
    expect(out).toContain("Withheld: its content was erased, or copies content that was erased since.");
    expect(out).not.toContain("Written by the author");
    expect(images(out)).toEqual([]);
  });

  describe("the reveal dialog", () => {
    const dialog = (reveal: Partial<NonNullable<CaseScreenViewProps["reveal"]>>) =>
      html(<RevealDialog reveal={{ itemId: ITEM_REPORTER, category: null, reason: "", busy: false, error: null, answer: null, ...reveal }} onChange={noop} onConfirm={noop} onClose={noop} />);
    const CONFIRM = />Confirm with your staff key<\/button>/;
    const CONFIRM_OFF = /<button type="button" class="primary" disabled=""[^>]*>Confirm with your staff key<\/button>/;

    test("opens on the item it was asked for, with the four reasons and none of them chosen, a reason text, and no other reveal to start meanwhile", () => {
      const asking = page(postCase(), { reveal: { itemId: ITEM_REPORTER, category: null, reason: "", busy: false, error: null, answer: null } });
      expect(asking.match(/role="dialog"/g)).toHaveLength(1);
      // Nothing is chosen for the person: the list opens on a line that is no reason.
      expect(asking).toContain('<option value="" disabled="" selected="">Choose why</option>');
      const reasons = { impersonation_claim: "A claim of impersonation", abuse_of_reporting: "Abuse of reporting", legal_requirement: "A legal requirement", other: "Another reason" };
      for (const [value, words] of Object.entries(reasons)) expect(asking).toContain(`<option value="${value}">${words}</option>`);
      expect(asking).toContain('<textarea id="reveal-reason"');
      // While one reveal is open no other can be started.
      expect(asking.match(/>Reveal who sent this<\/button>/g)).toHaveLength(2);
      expect(asking.match(/disabled="">Reveal who sent this<\/button>/g)).toHaveLength(2);
    });

    test("is confirmed with the key only once a reason is chosen and one is written: until then the button is off", () => {
      expect(dialog({})).toMatch(CONFIRM_OFF);
      expect(dialog({ category: "other" })).toMatch(CONFIRM_OFF);
      expect(dialog({ reason: "The reporter claims to be impersonated." })).toMatch(CONFIRM_OFF);
      // White space is no reason.
      expect(dialog({ category: "other", reason: `  ${String.fromCharCode(10)} ` })).toMatch(CONFIRM_OFF);
      const ready = dialog({ category: "abuse_of_reporting", reason: "The same account reported forty posts in an hour." });
      expect(ready).toMatch(CONFIRM);
      expect(ready).not.toMatch(CONFIRM_OFF);
      expect(ready).toContain('<option value="abuse_of_reporting" selected="">Abuse of reporting</option>');
      // Under way: off again, with the fields.
      expect(dialog({ category: "other", reason: "A reason.", busy: true })).toMatch(CONFIRM_OFF);
    });

    test("words a refusal in place, and keeps what was written", () => {
      const refused = dialog({ category: "other", reason: "As the reporter wrote: it is me.", error: messageFor("text_quotes_user") });
      expect(refused).toContain('<p role="alert" class="error">This text quotes what someone wrote about this case. Describe it in your own words, never copy it.</p>');
      expect(refused).toContain(">As the reporter wrote: it is me.</textarea>");
      expect(refused).toMatch(CONFIRM);
    });

    test("shows the answer in a frame of its own, the name alone as its text with its hidden characters to show, under a line of the console's that says what it is", () => {
      const label = '<p class="frame-label">Revealed to you; recorded and shown to every staff member</p>';
      const shown = dialog({ category: "other", reason: "x", answer: { handle: HOSTILE.script, name: null } });
      expect(shown).toContain(`<p>The reporter&#x27;s handle:</p><div class="frame">${label}<p class="frame-text"><bdi>${HOSTILE_ESCAPED.script}</bdi></p>`);
      expect(shown).toContain(">Show hidden characters</button>");
      expect(shown).not.toMatch(CONFIRM);
      expect(shown).toContain(">Close</button>");
      const named = dialog({ category: "other", reason: "x", answer: { handle: null, name: HOSTILE.bidi } });
      expect(named).toContain(`<p>The name the notifier gave:</p><div class="frame">${label}<p class="frame-text"><bdi>${HOSTILE.bidi}</bdi></p>`);
      // A name that was forgotten in between: nothing to frame, and the console says so.
      const forgotten = dialog({ category: "other", reason: "x", answer: { handle: null, name: null } });
      expect(forgotten).toContain("<p>The name is no longer kept, so nothing can be shown. The reveal is recorded all the same.</p>");
      expect(forgotten).not.toContain('class="frame"');
      expectInert(shown + named + forgotten);
    });

    test("the name is nowhere but in the open dialog: the case page without it, and the case's own answer, hold none of it", () => {
      const answer = { handle: "revealed_reporter_handle", name: null };
      const open = page(postCase(), { reveal: { itemId: ITEM_REPORTER, category: "other", reason: "x", busy: false, error: null, answer } });
      expect(open.split("revealed_reporter_handle").length - 1).toBe(1);
      // Closed, the page is the case as the API answers it, which never carries a source's name.
      expect(page(postCase(), { reveal: null })).not.toContain("revealed_reporter_handle");
      expect(JSON.stringify(postCase())).not.toContain("revealed_reporter_handle");
    });
  });
});

describe("saving a text", () => {
  const CASE = caseId(CASE_POST);
  const saved = { id: "8c9daebf-c0d1-42e3-845f-7a8b9cadbecf", digest: "cd".repeat(32) };

  test("the console trims the text, draws a 32-byte salt and sends the digest of exactly what it sends; what it answers is the digest it computed", async () => {
    const digest = await textDigest("ab".repeat(32), "Art. 18 check: no suspicion");
    const fake = fakeFetch({ [`POST /api/staff/cases/${CASE_POST}/texts`]: { status: 201, body: { id: saved.id, digest } } });
    const api = createStaffApi({ fetch: fake.fetch, cookie: () => "__Host-korbat_staff_csrf=t" });
    const random = (length: number) => new Uint8Array(length).fill(0xab);
    const answer = await saveStaffText({ api, random }, CASE, "note", "  Art. 18 check: no suspicion \n");
    expect(answer).toEqual({ id: saved.id, digest, text: "Art. 18 check: no suspicion", salt: "ab".repeat(32) });
    const sent = fake.requests[0]!.body as { kind: string; text: string; salt: string; digest: string };
    expect(sent).toEqual({ kind: "note", text: "Art. 18 check: no suspicion", salt: "ab".repeat(32), digest });
    expect(fake.requests[0]!.headers["x-staff-activity"]).toBe("1");
    expect(newSalt(random)).toBe("ab".repeat(32));
    expect(newSalt()).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/);
    expect(newSalt()).not.toBe(newSalt());
    // The composed form: a letter and its combining accent become the one letter.
    expect(normalised(`e${String.fromCharCode(0x301)} `)).toBe(String.fromCharCode(0xe9));
  });

  test("a text the rules refuse is never sent", async () => {
    const fake = fakeFetch({});
    const api = createStaffApi({ fetch: fake.fetch, cookie: () => "" });
    for (const text of ["x".repeat(5001), `a${String.fromCharCode(7)}b`, `a${String.fromCharCode(0x202e)}b`]) {
      await expect(saveStaffText({ api }, CASE, "reason", text)).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(TextRefused);
    }
    // Nor is a text of nothing or of white space alone, whatever its kind: the API takes none.
    for (const kind of ["note", "reveal_reason", "facts", "seal_declined"] as const) {
      for (const text of ["", "   ", ` ${String.fromCharCode(10)} `]) {
        await expect(saveStaffText({ api }, CASE, kind, text)).rejects.toMatchObject({ code: "invalid_request" });
      }
    }
    expect(fake.requests).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a save answered with another digest than the console computed is refused: the digest a confirmed action names is never one an answer carried", async () => {
    // The digest of a text the person never wrote, as an API under an attacker's control would answer it.
    const theirs = await textDigest("ab".repeat(32), "A reason the person never wrote.");
    const fake = fakeFetch({ [`POST /api/staff/cases/${CASE_POST}/texts`]: { status: 201, body: { id: saved.id, digest: theirs } } });
    const api = createStaffApi({ fetch: fake.fetch, cookie: () => "__Host-korbat_staff_csrf=t" });
    const refused = await saveStaffText({ api, random: (length) => new Uint8Array(length).fill(0xab) }, CASE, "reveal_reason", "What the person wrote.").catch((err: unknown) => err);
    expect(refused).toBeInstanceOf(ApiError);
    expect(refused).toMatchObject({ code: "invalid_answer", message: messageFor("invalid_answer") });
  });
});

describe("the reveal as the case page runs it: the reason saved first, then the key", () => {
  const CASE = caseId(CASE_POST);
  const REASON = "The same account reported forty posts of one author in an hour.";
  const SALT = "ab".repeat(32);
  const random = (length: number) => new Uint8Array(length).fill(0xab);
  const TEXTS = `POST /api/staff/cases/${CASE_POST}/texts`;
  const REVEAL = `POST /api/staff/items/${ITEM_REPORTER}/reveal`;

  async function run(table: Parameters<typeof fakeFetch>[0]) {
    const fake = fakeFetch({ "GET /api/staff/me": { status: 200, body: makeMe() }, ...table });
    const credentials = fakeCredentials();
    const api = createStaffApi({ fetch: fake.fetch, cookie: () => "__Host-korbat_staff_csrf=t" });
    const outcome = await revealSource({ api, credentials, random }, CASE, ITEM_REPORTER, "abuse_of_reporting", `  ${REASON} `);
    return { outcome, credentials, sent: fake.requests.map((request) => `${request.method} ${request.url}`), requests: fake.requests };
  }

  test("the key confirms the digest the console computed from what its person wrote, and the reveal carries it", async () => {
    const digest = await textDigest(SALT, REASON);
    const action = revealAction(ITEM_REPORTER, { reasonCategory: "abuse_of_reporting", reasonDigest: digest });
    const ran = await run({
      [TEXTS]: { status: 201, body: { id: "8c9daebf-c0d1-42e3-845f-7a8b9cadbecf", digest } },
      "POST /api/staff/step-up/options": { status: 200, body: stepUpOptions(await stepUpChallenge(SESSION_HANDLE, action)) },
      [REVEAL]: { status: 200, body: { handle: "some_reporter", name: null } },
    });
    expect(ran.outcome).toEqual({ answer: { handle: "some_reporter", name: null } });
    expect(ran.sent).toEqual([TEXTS, "GET /api/staff/me", "POST /api/staff/step-up/options", REVEAL]);
    expect(ran.requests[0]!.body).toEqual({ kind: "reveal_reason", text: REASON, salt: SALT, digest });
    expect(ran.requests[2]!.body).toEqual(action);
    expect(ran.requests[3]!.body).toMatchObject({ reasonCategory: "abuse_of_reporting", reasonDigest: digest });
    expect(ran.credentials.calls).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test("a save answered with another text's digest ends the reveal there: the key is never asked, and no options and no reveal are sent", async () => {
    const theirs = await textDigest(SALT, "A reason the person never wrote.");
    // Options that bind the reveal under the answered digest stand ready: a console that built its action from the answer
    // would find them in order and ask the key.
    const forged = revealAction(ITEM_REPORTER, { reasonCategory: "abuse_of_reporting", reasonDigest: theirs });
    const ran = await run({
      [TEXTS]: { status: 201, body: { id: "8c9daebf-c0d1-42e3-845f-7a8b9cadbecf", digest: theirs } },
      "POST /api/staff/step-up/options": { status: 200, body: stepUpOptions(await stepUpChallenge(SESSION_HANDLE, forged)) },
      [REVEAL]: { status: 200, body: { handle: "some_reporter", name: null } },
    });
    expect(ran.outcome).toEqual({ error: messageFor("invalid_answer") });
    expect(ran.credentials.calls).toEqual([]);
    expect(ran.sent).toEqual([TEXTS]);
  });

  test("each step's refusal is worded as that step's: the minute's limit on saved texts is never told as the day's limit on reveals", async () => {
    const digest = await textDigest(SALT, REASON);
    const action = revealAction(ITEM_REPORTER, { reasonCategory: "abuse_of_reporting", reasonDigest: digest });
    // The save is refused: nothing after it is sent.
    const saving = await run({ [TEXTS]: { status: 429, body: envelope("rate_limited") } });
    expect(saving.outcome).toEqual({ error: "Too many texts were saved in a minute. Wait a moment and save again." });
    expect(saving.outcome).toEqual({ error: NOTE_WORDS.rate_limited });
    expect(saving.sent).toEqual([TEXTS]);
    expect(saving.credentials.calls).toEqual([]);
    // The reveal is refused, once the key confirmed it.
    const revealing = await run({
      [TEXTS]: { status: 201, body: { id: "8c9daebf-c0d1-42e3-845f-7a8b9cadbecf", digest } },
      "POST /api/staff/step-up/options": { status: 200, body: stepUpOptions(await stepUpChallenge(SESSION_HANDLE, action)) },
      [REVEAL]: { status: 429, body: envelope("rate_limited") },
    });
    expect(revealing.outcome).toEqual({ error: "You have revealed as many sources as one staff account may in a day. You can reveal others after midnight UTC." });
    expect(revealing.outcome).toEqual({ error: REVEAL_WORDS.rate_limited });
    expect(revealing.credentials.calls).toHaveLength(1);
    // A text that quotes a reporter is refused at the save, in the words every screen has for it.
    const quoting = await run({ [TEXTS]: { status: 422, body: envelope("text_quotes_user") } });
    expect(quoting.outcome).toEqual({ error: MODERATION_MESSAGES.text_quotes_user });
  });
});

describe("reading the case again", () => {
  const read: CaseView = postCase();
  const refused = (code: string) => Object.assign(new Error("the server's own words"), { code });

  test("only the first read may put the page into its failed state: a later read that fails keeps the page as it is and says why on its error line", () => {
    // The first read: there is no page to keep.
    expect(afterFailedRead({ state: "loading" }, refused("staff_recused"))).toEqual({ view: { state: "failed", message: MODERATION_MESSAGES.staff_recused }, error: null });
    expect(afterFailedRead({ state: "loading" }, refused("rate_limited"))).toEqual({ view: { state: "failed", message: CASE_WORDS.rate_limited }, error: null });
    // A read after a snapshot, a note or a reveal: the case stays on the page, the name a reveal just showed with it.
    const shown = { state: "ready" as const, value: read };
    const kept = afterFailedRead(shown, refused("staff_recused"));
    expect(kept.view).toBe(shown);
    expect(kept.error).toBe(MODERATION_MESSAGES.staff_recused);
    expect(afterFailedRead(shown, new Error("no code at all"))).toEqual({ view: shown, error: "Something went wrong. Try again." });
    // The words are the console's own, on either line.
    expect(JSON.stringify([kept, afterFailedRead({ state: "loading" }, refused("not_found"))])).not.toContain("the server's own words");
    expect(afterFailedRead({ state: "loading" }, refused("not_found")).view).toEqual({ state: "failed", message: "No case has this address." });
  });

  test("a refused case read is worded by the console, never by the server: the API's client drops the server's message, and the page shows the console's words for the code", async () => {
    const fake = fakeFetch({ [`GET /api/staff/cases/${CASE_POST}`]: { status: 403, body: envelope("staff_recused", "the server's own words") } });
    const api = createStaffApi({ fetch: fake.fetch, cookie: () => "" });
    const err = await api.caseView(caseId(CASE_POST), { activity: true }).catch((thrown: unknown) => thrown);
    expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(ApiError);
    expect(err).toMatchObject({ status: 403, code: "staff_recused", message: MODERATION_MESSAGES.staff_recused });
    const failed = afterFailedRead({ state: "loading" }, err);
    const out = html(<Loaded value={failed.view} render={() => null} />);
    expect(out).toBe(`<p class="error">${MODERATION_MESSAGES.staff_recused}</p>`);
    expect(out).not.toContain("the server's own words");
    // The day's limit on cases has words of its own on this page.
    const limit = fakeFetch({ [`GET /api/staff/cases/${CASE_POST}`]: { status: 429, body: envelope("rate_limited", "the server's own words") } });
    const limited = await createStaffApi({ fetch: limit.fetch, cookie: () => "" })
      .caseView(caseId(CASE_POST), { activity: true })
      .catch((thrown: unknown) => thrown);
    expect(afterFailedRead({ state: "loading" }, limited).view).toEqual({
      state: "failed",
      message: "You have opened as many different cases as one staff account may in a day. You can open others after midnight UTC; every staff account has been told.",
    });
  });
});

describe("the reveal, confirmed by the key", () => {
  const params = { reasonCategory: "impersonation_claim" as const, reasonDigest: "cd".repeat(32) };
  const action = revealAction(ITEM_REPORTER, params);

  async function revealWith(options: unknown) {
    const fake = fakeFetch({
      "GET /api/staff/me": { status: 200, body: makeMe() },
      "POST /api/staff/step-up/options": { status: 200, body: options },

    });

    const outcome = await revealWithKey({ api, credentials }, ITEM_REPORTER, params).catch((err: unknown) => err);
    return { outcome, credentials, requests: fake.requests };
  }

  test("the action is the item with the reason's category and digest, and nothing typed", () => {
    expect(action).toEqual({ action: "identity_revealed", target: { type: "intake_item", id: ITEM_REPORTER }, params });
    expect(() => revealAction(ITEM_REPORTER.toUpperCase(), params)).toThrow();
    expect(() => revealAction(ITEM_REPORTER, { ...params, reason: "free text" } as never)).toThrow();
  });

  test("options bound to exactly this reveal are signed, and the reveal is sent with the params and the assertion", async () => {
    const run = await revealWith(stepUpOptions(await stepUpChallenge(SESSION_HANDLE, action)));
    expect(run.outcome).toEqual({ handle: "some_reporter", name: null });
    expect(run.credentials.calls).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(run.requests.map((request) => `${request.method} ${request.url} ${request.headers["x-staff-activity"]}`)).toEqual([
      "GET /api/staff/me 1",
      "POST /api/staff/step-up/options 1",
      `POST /api/staff/items/${ITEM_REPORTER}/reveal 1`,
    ]);
    expect(run.requests[1]!.body).toEqual(action);
    expect(run.requests[2]!.body).toMatchObject({ ...params, stepUp: { type: "public-key" } });
  });

  test("options that bind another item, other params or another action are refused before the key is asked, and nothing is sent", async () => {
    const others = [
      revealAction(ITEM_NOTIFIER, params),
      revealAction(ITEM_REPORTER, { ...params, reasonCategory: "other" }),
      revealAction(ITEM_REPORTER, { ...params, reasonDigest: "ef".repeat(32) }),
      { action: "staff_session_revoked", target: { type: "staff_session", id: ITEM_REPORTER }, params: {} },
    ];
    for (const other of others) {
      const run = await revealWith(stepUpOptions(await stepUpChallenge(SESSION_HANDLE, other)));
      expect(run.outcome).toBeInstanceOf(StepUpMismatch);
      expect(run.credentials.calls).toEqual([]);
      expect(run.requests.map((request) => request.url)).toEqual(["/api/staff/me", "/api/staff/step-up/options"]);
    }
  });
});

    const store = createConsoleStore({ api, clock: new FakeClock(), path: "/queue", history: { pushState: (_data, _unused, url) => void pushed.push(url), replaceState: noop } });

});
```

```tsx
  expect(out).toContain(`<bdi>${HOSTILE.bidi}</bdi>`);
}

  });

  test("no sign-ins, and lists still loading or failed", () => {
    const out = html(<HomeView {...props} signIns={{ state: "ready", value: [] }} sessions={{ state: "loading" }} keys={{ state: "failed", message: "Cannot reach the server." }} />);
    expect(out).toContain("No staff sign-ins in the last 7 days.");
    expect(out).toContain("Loading");
    expect(out).toContain("Cannot reach the server.");
  });

  test("opened 11 hours after the page read its session, it lists sign-ins back to 7 days before its own opening", async () => {
    // The page read its session at 09:00 and its person kept acting, so the idle timer never read /me again: the session
    // the page holds still says 09:00 when Home opens at 20:00.
    const pageOpened = Date.parse("2026-10-01T09:00:00.000Z");
    const homeOpened = Date.parse("2026-10-01T20:00:00.000Z");
    const at = (createdAt: string, seq: number): AuditEntry => ({ ...signIn("mod_anna", seq), createdAt });
    const fake = fakeFetch({
      "GET /api/staff/me": [{ status: 200, body: makeMe({ at: pageOpened }) }, { status: 200, body: makeMe({ at: homeOpened, absolute: 3600 }) }],
      "GET /api/staff/audit?action=staff_sign_in": {
        status: 200,
        body: {
          entries: [
            at("2026-10-01T19:00:00.000Z", 40),
            at("2026-09-24T20:30:00.000Z", 39),
            // Older than 7 days at 20:00, though not at the page's stale 09:00: the list ends before it.
            at("2026-09-24T19:30:00.000Z", 38),
            at("2026-09-24T09:30:00.000Z", 37),
          ],
          nextCursor: 37,
        },
      },
      "GET /api/staff/sessions": { status: 200, body: { sessions: [] } },
      "GET /api/staff/keys": { status: 200, body: { keys: [] } },
      "GET /api/staff/overview": { status: 200, body: QUIET },
    });
    const api = createStaffApi({ fetch: fake.fetch, cookie: () => "" });
    const store = createConsoleStore({ api, clock: new FakeClock(), path: "/", history: { pushState: noop, replaceState: noop } });
    await store.start();
    const held = store.get().session;
    if (held.kind !== "signed-in") throw new Error("the page holds no session");
    expect(serverNow(held.me)).toBe(pageOpened);

    // What the screen runs when it opens, with the session the page holds as its `me`.
    let signIns: Loadable<AuditEntry[]> = { state: "loading" };
    openHome(api, { current: true }, { overview: noop, signIns: (value) => (signIns = value), sessions: noop, keys: noop });
    await settle();
    expect(signIns).toMatchObject({ state: "ready" });
    const out = html(<HomeView {...props} me={held.me} signIns={signIns} />);
    expect(out).toContain("2026-10-01 19:00");
    expect(out).toContain("2026-09-24 20:30");
    expect(out).not.toContain("2026-09-24 19:30");
    expect(out).not.toContain("2026-09-24 09:30");
    // The screen's own /me, marked as its person's opening of it, came before the first page of sign-ins.
    const asked = fake.requests.map((r) => `${r.url} ${r.headers["x-staff-activity"]}`);
    expect(asked.filter((r) => r.startsWith("/api/staff/me"))).toEqual(["/api/staff/me 1", "/api/staff/me 1"]);
    expect(asked.indexOf("/api/staff/audit?action=staff_sign_in 1")).toBeGreaterThan(asked.lastIndexOf("/api/staff/me 1"));
    store.dispose();
  });
});
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/account/deletion.test.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import pino from "pino";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import type { AccountDeps } from "../../src/account/context";
import { confirmDeletion, purge, startDeletion } from "../../src/account/flows/deletion";
import { PURGE_INTERVAL_MS, createPurgeJob, purgePending } from "../../src/account/purge";
import { AuthError, type Session } from "../../src/auth";
import type { RequestContext } from "../../src/auth/context";
import { randomToken, sha256Hex } from "../../src/auth/crypto";
import { MemoryJobLock } from "../../src/lib/jobs";
import { MemoryStore } from "../../src/middleware/rate-limit";

const T0 = 1_789_000_000_000;

interface LogLine {
  level: number;
  msg: string;
  userId?: string;
  purged?: number;
  failed?: number;
}

/**
 * The deletion flows and the purge job on stateful fakes of the three module interfaces: the auth
 * fake knows one account whose handle is "ada" and keeps deleted_at and purged_at per account; the
 * social fake keeps which profiles were purged and can be told to fail once for an account, before its
 * transaction does anything or at its commit (which puts back the image rows the transaction took, as a
 * rollback would); the media fake holds image ids per owner and hands them out once. Every call is
 * logged in order, the commit of the social purge's transaction included, and the transaction it opens
 * is a sentinel the media fake must be handed.
 */
function harness() {
  let t = T0;
  const calls: string[] = [];
  const lines: LogLine[] = [];
  const users = new Map<string, { deletedAt: Date | null; purgedAt: Date | null }>();
  const purgedProfiles = new Map<string, Date>();
  const failing = new Set<string>();
  const failingCommit = new Set<string>();
  const images = new Map<string, string[]>();
  const requested: string[][] = [];
  const started: { session: Session; ctx: RequestContext }[] = [];
  const tx = { sentinel: randomUUID() } as unknown as DbTx;
  const seenTx: unknown[] = [];
  const deps: AccountDeps = {
    auth: {
      startDeletion: async (session, ctx) => {
        calls.push("auth.startDeletion");
        started.push({ session, ctx });
        return { flowId: `flow-${session.userId}` };
      },
      confirmDeletion: async (session, input) => {
        calls.push("auth.confirmDeletion");
        if (input.handle.toLowerCase() !== "ada") throw new AuthError("invalid_request", 400, "handle_mismatch");
        const user = users.get(session.userId);
        if (!user || user.deletedAt) throw new AuthError("invalid_credentials", 401);
        user.deletedAt = new Date(t);
      },
      pendingPurges: async () => {
        calls.push("auth.pendingPurges");
        return [...users].filter(([, user]) => user.deletedAt && !user.purgedAt).map(([id]) => id);
      },
      finishPurge: async (userId) => {
        calls.push("auth.finishPurge");
        const user = users.get(userId);
        // As the real statement: a row already purged, or never deleted, is left alone.
        if (user?.deletedAt && !user.purgedAt) user.purgedAt = new Date(t);
      },
      exportAccount: async () => {
        throw new Error("not exercised here");
      },
      appendEvent: async () => undefined,
    },
    social: {
      purgeProfile: async (userId, now, within) => {
        calls.push("social.purgeProfile");
        if (failing.delete(userId)) throw new Error("the social purge failed");
        const rowsBefore = images.get(userId);
        await within(tx);
        if (failingCommit.delete(userId)) {
          calls.push("social.rollback");
          if (rowsBefore) images.set(userId, rowsBefore);
          throw new Error("the social purge's commit failed");
        }
        calls.push("social.commit");
        if (!purgedProfiles.has(userId)) purgedProfiles.set(userId, now);
      },
      exportProfile: async () => {
        throw new Error("not exercised here");
      },
    },
    media: {
      purgeOwner: async (within, ownerId) => {
        calls.push("media.purgeOwner");
        seenTx.push(within);
        const ids = images.get(ownerId) ?? [];
        images.delete(ownerId);
        return ids;
      },
      requestDeletion: async (ids) => {
        calls.push(`media.requestDeletion(${ids.length})`);
        requested.push([...ids]);
      },
      exportImages: async () => [],
    },
    limits: new MemoryStore(() => t),
    log: pino({ level: "info" }, { write: (line: string) => void lines.push(JSON.parse(line) as LogLine) }),
    now: () => new Date(t),
  };
  /** An onboarded account, live unless told otherwise, with a session that just proved a credential. */
  function account(options: { deletedAt?: Date; images?: string[] } = {}): { userId: string; session: Session } {
    const userId = randomUUID();
    users.set(userId, { deletedAt: options.deletedAt ?? null, purgedAt: null });
    if (options.images) images.set(userId, options.images);
    const session: Session = {
      sessionId: sha256Hex(randomToken()),
      userId,
      deviceId: randomUUID(),
      role: "user",
      onboarded: true,
      mfaEnabled: false,
      reauthAt: new Date(t),
      handle: randomUUID(),
      factors: { email: t },
      passkeyId: null,
    };
    return { userId, session };
  }
  const ctx: RequestContext = { ipHash: randomToken(), userAgent: "test" };
  return {
    deps,
    calls,
    lines,
    users,
    purgedProfiles,
    failing,
    failingCommit,
    images,
    requested,
    started,
    tx,
    seenTx,
    ctx,
    account,
    now: () => new Date(t),
    advance(ms: number) {
      t += ms;
    },
  };
}

describe("account deletion: the flows", () => {
  test("the start step hands the session and the request context to the auth module and answers its flow id", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account();
    expect(await startDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, h.ctx)).toEqual({ flowId: `flow-${ada.userId}` });
    expect(h.started).toEqual([{ session: ada.session, ctx: h.ctx }]);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.startDeletion"]);
  });

  test("confirming runs the auth confirmation, then the social purge with the media detach and the file deletion requests inside its transaction, then the auth purge, in that order", async () => {
    const h = harness();

    const ada = h.account({ images: [imageA, imageB] });
    await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId: "f", code: "123456", handle: "Ada" });
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.confirmDeletion", "social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "media.requestDeletion(2)", "social.commit", "auth.finishPurge"]);
    // The image rows go in the social purge's own transaction, and their files are asked for by id before it commits,
    // so no run can commit the rows away and then stop before asking.
    expect(h.seenTx).toEqual([h.tx]);
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([[imageA, imageB]]);
    expect(h.purgedProfiles.get(ada.userId)).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)).toEqual({ deletedAt: h.now(), purgedAt: h.now() });
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.lines.filter((line) => line.level >= 40)).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a refused confirmation purges nothing", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ images: [randomUUID()] });
    const refused = await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId: "f", code: "123456", handle: "not_ada" }).catch((err: unknown) => err);
    expect(refused).toBeInstanceOf(AuthError);
    expect((refused as AuthError).message).toBe("handle_mismatch");
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.confirmDeletion"]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)).toEqual({ deletedAt: null, purgedAt: null });
    expect(h.images.get(ada.userId)).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  test("a purge that fails after the confirmation is logged and the confirmation still succeeds; the account stays pending for the job", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ images: [randomUUID()] });
    h.failing.add(ada.userId);
    await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId: "f", code: "123456", handle: "ada" });
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.confirmDeletion", "social.purgeProfile"]);
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)).toEqual({ deletedAt: h.now(), purgedAt: null });
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    const errors = h.lines.filter((line) => line.level >= 50);
    expect(errors).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(errors[0]!.userId).toBe(ada.userId);
    expect(errors[0]!.msg).toMatch(/purge/);
  });

  test("the purge is safe to repeat: a second run detaches nothing, requests no deletion, and leaves the purged row as it was", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000), images: [randomUUID()] });
    await purge(h.deps, ada.userId);
    const first = { ...h.users.get(ada.userId)!, profilePurgedAt: h.purgedProfiles.get(ada.userId) };
    expect(first).toEqual({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000), purgedAt: h.now(), profilePurgedAt: h.now() });
    h.calls.length = 0;
    h.advance(60_000);
    await purge(h.deps, ada.userId);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "media.requestDeletion(0)", "social.commit", "auth.finishPurge"]);
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([[expect.any(String)], []]);
    expect({ ...h.users.get(ada.userId)!, profilePurgedAt: h.purgedProfiles.get(ada.userId) }).toEqual(first);
  });

  test("a purge whose transaction fails at the commit has already asked for the files; the next run finds the rows again and asks for the same ids", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const [imageA, imageB] = [randomUUID(), randomUUID()];
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000), images: [imageA, imageB] });
    h.failingCommit.add(ada.userId);
    await expect(purge(h.deps, ada.userId)).rejects.toThrow(/commit/);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "media.requestDeletion(2)", "social.rollback"]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toBeNull();
    // The requests are one per id, so asking again for the same ids changes nothing on disk.

  });
});

describe("the purge job", () => {
  test("purges every pending account, counts the ones that failed, and finishes on the next round what failed once", async () => {
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 120_000), images: [randomUUID()] });
    const bob = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000) });
    h.account();
    h.failing.add(ada.userId);

    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 1 });
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toBeNull();
    expect(h.users.get(bob.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    // The failure is logged with the account, and the round with its counts.
    expect(h.lines.filter((line) => line.level >= 50).map((line) => line.userId)).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    expect(h.lines.filter((line) => line.purged !== undefined).map((line) => [line.purged, line.failed])).toEqual([[1, 1]]);

    h.advance(PURGE_INTERVAL_MS);
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 0 });
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(h.requested).toEqual([[], [expect.any(String)]]);
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([]);
    // A round with nothing to do reports zeros and logs nothing.
    h.lines.length = 0;
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 0, failed: 0 });
    expect(h.lines).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("runs every five minutes under the lock job:account-purge, and skips a round another instance holds", async () => {
    expect(PURGE_INTERVAL_MS).toBe(5 * 60_000);
    const h = harness();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000) });
    const lock = new MemoryJobLock(() => Date.now());
    const job = createPurgeJob(h.deps, lock);
    await lock.acquire("job:account-purge", "other", 10_000);
    expect(await job.round()).toBe("skipped");
    expect(h.calls).toEqual([]);
    await lock.release("job:account-purge", "other");
    expect(await job.round()).toBe("ran");
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
    expect(await lock.acquire("job:account-purge", "other", 10_000)).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("the purge and the reports the account sent (3c design, section 7.10)", () => {
  /** The harness with the moderation module's interface for this one: the forgetting is logged with the other calls, and can be made to fail. */
  function withModeration() {
    const h = harness();
    const forgotten: string[] = [];
    const failing = new Set<string>();
    h.deps.moderation = {
      forgetAccount: async (userId) => {
        h.calls.push("moderation.forgetAccount");
        if (failing.delete(userId)) throw new Error("the forgetting failed");
        forgotten.push(userId);
      },
    };
    return { ...h, forgotten, failingForget: failing };
  }

  test("the reporter links are forgotten after the social purge has committed and before the account counts as purged", async () => {
    const h = withModeration();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000), images: [randomUUID()] });
    await purge(h.deps, ada.userId);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "media.requestDeletion(1)", "social.commit", "moderation.forgetAccount", "auth.finishPurge"]);
    expect(h.forgotten).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
  });

  test("a forgetting that fails leaves the account pending, and the next run does every step again and finishes", async () => {
    const h = withModeration();
    const ada = h.account({ deletedAt: new Date(T0 - 60_000) });
    h.failingForget.add(ada.userId);
    await expect(purge(h.deps, ada.userId)).rejects.toThrow(/forgetting/);
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "media.requestDeletion(0)", "social.commit", "moderation.forgetAccount"]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toBeNull();
    expect(await h.deps.auth.pendingPurges()).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    // The job's next round: the same steps, and this time the account is purged.
    expect(await purgePending(h.deps)).toEqual({ purged: 1, failed: 0 });
    expect(h.forgotten).toEqual([ada.userId]);
    expect(h.users.get(ada.userId)!.purgedAt).toEqual(h.now());
  });

  test("the confirmation purges through the same steps: the owner's request answers once their reports are forgotten too", async () => {
    const h = withModeration();
    const ada = h.account();
    await confirmDeletion(h.deps, ada.session, { flowId: "f", code: "123456", handle: "ada" });
    expect(h.calls).toEqual(["auth.confirmDeletion", "social.purgeProfile", "media.purgeOwner", "media.requestDeletion(0)", "social.commit", "moderation.forgetAccount", "auth.finishPurge"]);
    expect(h.forgotten).toEqual([ada.userId]);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { join, posix, relative, sep } from "node:path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

/**
 * Module boundaries (1a spec section 2.2, 2a spec section 2.2, 3a design section 5, 3c design section 5). Paths are relative to apps/api/src
 * with forward slashes. The rules are plain functions so the tests below can prove each one catches
 * a deliberate violation.
 */
interface SourceFile {
  path: string;
  source: string;
}

const SRC_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../src", import.meta.url));
const SCHEMA_ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../../../packages/db/src/schema", import.meta.url));

/** Schema files that define auth-schema objects or shared helpers; every other schema file is public. */
const NON_PUBLIC_SCHEMA_FILES = new Set(["auth.ts", "helpers.ts", "index.ts"]);
const AUTH_SCHEMA_FILE = "auth.ts";
// The command lines open both pools: grant-role changes a role on the auth pool, and staff.js reads there the staff keys
// that audit-verify checks the record against.
const AUTH_POOL_ALLOWED = new Set(["config.ts", "index.ts", "cli/grant-role.ts", "cli/staff.ts"]);
const AUTH_KEYS_ALLOWED = new Set(["config.ts"]);

/** Modules that may only be entered through their index file. */
const MODULES = ["auth", "social", "media", "account", "staff", "moderation"] as const;

function walk(dir: string): string[] {
  return readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).flatMap((entry) => {
    const full = join(dir, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) return walk(full);
    return entry.name.endsWith(".ts") ? [full] : [];
  });
}

function loadSources(): SourceFile[] {
  return walk(SRC_ROOT).map((full) => ({ path: relative(SRC_ROOT, full).split(sep).join("/"), source: readFileSync(full, "utf8") }));
}

function exportedNames(file: string): string[] {
  const source = readFileSync(join(SCHEMA_ROOT, file), "utf8");
  return [...source.matchAll(/^export (?:const|function|type|interface|enum) ([A-Za-z0-9_]+)/gm)].map((m) => m[1]!);
}

/** Names exported by the public-schema files of @korbat/db (tables and enums the auth module must not touch). */
function publicSchemaNames(): Set<string> {
  const names = new Set<string>();
  for (const file of readdirSync(SCHEMA_ROOT)) {
    if (!file.endsWith(".ts") || NON_PUBLIC_SCHEMA_FILES.has(file)) continue;
    for (const name of exportedNames(file)) names.add(name);
  }
  return names;
}

/** Names exported by the auth-schema file of @korbat/db (tables and enums the social module must not touch). */
function authSchemaNames(): Set<string> {
  return new Set(exportedNames(AUTH_SCHEMA_FILE));
}

/** Every module specifier in static imports, re-exports, side-effect imports and dynamic imports. */
function specifiers(source: string): string[] {
  return [...source.matchAll(/(?:\bfrom\s+|\bimport\s*\(\s*|\bimport\s+)["']([^"']+)["']/g)].map((m) => m[1]!);
}

/** Named bindings of every `import { ... } from "@korbat/db"`; a namespace import yields the marker "*". */
function dbImports(source: string): string[] {
  const names: string[] = [];
  for (const match of source.matchAll(/\bimport\s+(type\s+)?(\*\s+as\s+\w+|\{[^}]*\})\s+from\s+["'](@korbat\/db(?:\/[^"']*)?)["']/g)) {
    const bindings = match[2]!;
    if (bindings.startsWith("*")) {
      names.push("*");
      continue;
    }
    for (const part of bindings.slice(1, -1).split(",")) {
      const name = part.trim().replace(/^type\s+/, "").split(/\s+as\s+/)[0]!.trim();
      if (name) names.push(name);
    }
  }
  return names;
}

const insideAuth = (path: string) => path.startsWith("auth/");
const insideSocial = (path: string) => path.startsWith("social/");
const insideMedia = (path: string) => path.startsWith("media/");
const insideAccount = (path: string) => path.startsWith("account/");
const insideStaff = (path: string) => path.startsWith("staff/");
const insideModeration = (path: string) => path.startsWith("moderation/");

function findViolations(files: SourceFile[], publicNames: Set<string>, authNames: Set<string>): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    for (const spec of specifiers(source)) {
      if (!spec.startsWith(".")) continue;
      const target = posix.normalize(posix.join(posix.dirname(path), spec)).replace(/\.ts$/, "");
      for (const module of MODULES) {
        if (path.startsWith(`${module}/`)) continue;
        if (target.startsWith(`${module}/`) && target !== `${module}/index`) {
          violations.push(`${path}: imports ${spec}, which is inside the ${module} module (use ./${module})`);
        }
      }
    }
    if (!insideAuth(path) && !AUTH_POOL_ALLOWED.has(path) && /\b(DATABASE_URL_AUTH|authDb)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references the auth database pool`);
    }
    // Each encryption key with the list of the keys it replaced: after a rotation those still open what was stored before it.
    if (!insideAuth(path) && !AUTH_KEYS_ALLOWED.has(path) && /\b(TOTP_ENC_KEY|TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS|NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY|NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS|AUTH_HMAC_KEY|IP_HASH_KEY)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references an auth key`);
    }
    if (insideAuth(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (import auth-schema names explicitly)`);
        else if (publicNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports public-schema ${name} from @korbat/db`);
      }
    }
    if (!insideMedia(path) && /\b(postMedia|post_media)\b/.test(source)) {
      violations.push(`${path}: references post_media, which only the media module may touch`);
    }
    // The staff module (role korbat_api) reads and writes the public audit log; staff keys, staff sessions and enrolments
    // are credentials, the auth module's alone (3a design, section 5). The moderation module owns the moderation tables on
    // the same role: a notifier's contact and the staff links live in the auth schema, out of its reach (3c design, section 5).
    if (insideSocial(path) || insideMedia(path) || insideStaff(path) || insideModeration(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (import public-schema names explicitly)`);
        else if (authNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports auth-schema ${name} from @korbat/db`);
      }
    }
    // The account module sequences the other three through their index files and holds no table access of its own
    // (1b spec, section 5): no table or enum of either schema may be named in it. Db and DbTx, which are not schema
    // names, stay allowed, since a transaction is passed through it.
    if (insideAccount(path)) {
      for (const name of dbImports(source)) {
        if (name === "*") violations.push(`${path}: namespace import of @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
        else if (publicNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports public-schema ${name} from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
        else if (authNames.has(name)) violations.push(`${path}: imports auth-schema ${name} from @korbat/db (the account module holds no table access)`);
      }
    }
    // The staff module uses the auth module's interface as the other modules do, never its repository or its session
    // store, which would hand it the auth tables; the moderation module likewise. Any mention counts, so a renamed,
    // namespace or dynamic import is caught as surely as a named one.
    if (insideStaff(path) || insideModeration(path)) {
      const module = insideStaff(path) ? "staff" : "moderation";
      for (const name of new Set([...source.matchAll(/\b(createAuthRepo|createSessions)\b/g)].map((m) => m[1]!))) {
        violations.push(`${path}: uses the auth module's ${name} (the ${module} module goes through the auth module's interface)`);
      }
    }
  }
  return violations;
}

/**
 * The source pins of the freeze (3c design, sections 6.1 and 6.5). The freeze of the path for suspected child sexual abuse
 * material holds only while every path of a kind passes one gate, so who may name what is pinned here, beside the
 * database's own pins of who names the predicate there:
 *   - `post_frozen` is named only in the media repository and the moderation repository, and `frozen_for` nowhere in the
 *     API: no other file decides by itself what is frozen;
 *   - a delete of `post_media` is written only in the media repository, whose every delete the keep trigger judges and
 *     whose every answer names only rows that are gone;
 *   - `requestDeletion` (asking the worker to delete an image's files) and `openImage` (opening an image file of the
 *     store) are named in a pinned list of files, each a pinned number of times, comments included: a new caller of
 *     either fails the test until whoever adds it has checked it against the gates and listed it.
 */
const POST_FROZEN_ALLOWED = new Set(["media/repo.ts", "moderation/repo.ts"]);
const POST_MEDIA_DELETE_ALLOWED = new Set(["media/repo.ts"]);
const POST_MEDIA_DELETE = /\bdelete\s+from\s+(?:only\s+)?(?:"?public"?\s*\.\s*)?"?post_media\b|\btruncate\b[^;`]*\bpost_media\b|\.delete\(\s*postMedia\b/i;

function findFreezeViolations(files: SourceFile[]): string[] {
  const violations: string[] = [];
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    if (/\bfrozen_for\b/.test(source)) violations.push(`${path}: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name`);
    if (/\bpost_frozen\b/.test(source) && !POST_FROZEN_ALLOWED.has(path)) violations.push(`${path}: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may`);
    if (POST_MEDIA_DELETE.test(source) && !POST_MEDIA_DELETE_ALLOWED.has(path)) violations.push(`${path}: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may`);
  }
  return violations;
}

/** Every file that names `name` as a whole word, with how often, comments included. */
function mentions(files: SourceFile[], name: string): Record<string, number> {
  const found: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const { path, source } of files) {
    // Cut at every word boundary: a whole word is then a piece of its own.
    const count = source.split(/\b/).filter((piece) => piece === name).length;
    if (count > 0) found[path] = count;
  }
  return found;
}

/**
 * Where `requestDeletion` is named. A deletion request names an id that a delete of post_media answered, an upload that
 * failed before it could be put on a post, or a file that has no row: the files module writes the request; the upload's
 * removal, the sweeper, the author's deletion (after its commit), the account's purge (inside its transaction) and the
 * disposal's caller (after its commit) ask for it through the module's interfaces.
 */
const REQUEST_DELETION = {
  "account/flows/deletion.ts": 1,
  "media/cases.ts": 4,
  "media/context.ts": 2,
  "media/files.ts": 1,
  "media/flows/remove.ts": 1,
  "media/index.ts": 5,
  "media/sweeper.ts": 2,
  // The retention job, which asks for a batch's files after the commit of the transaction that deleted their rows.
  "moderation/retention.ts": 1,
  "social/context.ts": 1,
  "social/flows/posts.ts": 1,
};

/**
 * Where `openImage` is named: the files module, which opens a file of the store under its checks, and its three callers,
 * each behind its own reader's rule: serve (gate S), the export's open (which reads the row again) and the staff's image
 * (gate V).
 */
const OPEN_IMAGE = {
  "media/cases.ts": 1,
  "media/files.ts": 1,
  "media/flows/serve.ts": 1,
  "media/index.ts": 1,
};

describe("the freeze's source pins", () => {
  test("apps/api/src names post_frozen only in the two repositories, frozen_for nowhere, and deletes from post_media only in the media repository", () => {
    expect(findFreezeViolations(loadSources())).toEqual([]);
    // The media repository does name the predicate and does delete: the pins are about a file that exists.
    const repo = loadSources().find((file) => file.path === "media/repo.ts")!;
    expect(repo.source).toMatch(/\bpost_frozen\b/);
    expect(POST_MEDIA_DELETE.test(repo.source)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("catches the predicate named outside the two repositories, and its core named anywhere", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "sql`select public.post_frozen(m.post_id) as frozen from post_media m`" },
      { path: "moderation/repo.ts", source: "sql`select not public.post_frozen(${postId}::uuid) as images_allowed`" },
      { path: "moderation/cases.ts", source: "const [row] = await tx.execute(sql`select public.post_frozen(${postId}::uuid) as frozen`);" },
      { path: "media/flows/serve.ts", source: "const frozen = await db.execute(sql`select post_frozen(${postId})`);" },
      { path: "staff/cases.ts", source: "await db.execute(sql`select public.frozen_for(${postId}::uuid, ${authorId}::uuid)`);" },
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "sql`select public.frozen_for(m.post_id, m.owner_id) from post_media m`" },
      // Another word that only contains the name is not the name.
      { path: "social/views.ts", source: "const post_frozen_label = 1; const unfrozen_for_now = 2;" },
    ];
    expect(findFreezeViolations(files)).toEqual([
      "moderation/cases.ts: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may",
      "media/flows/serve.ts: names post_frozen, which only the media and moderation repositories may",
      "staff/cases.ts: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name",
      "media/repo.ts: names frozen_for, which only the database's own functions name",
    ]);
  });

  test("catches a delete of post_media outside the media repository, in SQL and through the query builder", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "media/repo.ts", source: "await tx.execute(sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where post_id = ${postId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`);\nawait db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));" },
      { path: "media/sweeper.ts", source: "await db.execute(sql`delete from post_media where post_id is null and created_at < ${before}`);" },
      { path: "media/flows/remove.ts", source: "await deps.db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));" },
      { path: "media/cases.ts", source: 'await tx.execute(sql`DELETE FROM "public"."post_media" WHERE "id" = ${id}`);' },
      { path: "media/index.ts", source: "await tx.execute(sql`truncate table post_media cascade`);" },
      // Reading and updating image rows, and deleting something else, is not a delete of image rows.
      { path: "media/flows/status.ts", source: "await db.update(postMedia).set({ status }).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));\nawait db.delete(posts).where(eq(posts.id, id));\nconst rows = await db.execute(sql`select id from post_media`);" },
    ];
    expect(findFreezeViolations(files)).toEqual([
      "media/sweeper.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/flows/remove.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/cases.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
      "media/index.ts: deletes from post_media, which only the media repository may",
    ]);
  });

  test("requestDeletion and openImage are named in exactly the pinned files, each the pinned number of times", () => {
    expect(mentions(loadSources(), "requestDeletion")).toEqual(REQUEST_DELETION);
    expect(mentions(loadSources(), "openImage")).toEqual(OPEN_IMAGE);
  });

  test("catches a new caller of either, in a file of the list and in one outside it", () => {
    const real = loadSources();
    // A second request in the purge's flow, and a first one in a file that had none.
    const withCallers = real
      .map((file) => (file.path === "account/flows/deletion.ts" ? { ...file, source: `${file.source}\nawait deps.media.requestDeletion(kept);` } : file))
      .concat([{ path: "moderation/decide.ts", source: "await deps.media.requestDeletion(ids);" }]);
    expect(mentions(withCallers, "requestDeletion")).not.toEqual(REQUEST_DELETION);
    expect(mentions(withCallers, "requestDeletion")).toMatchObject({ "account/flows/deletion.ts": 2, "moderation/decide.ts": 1 });
    // A fourth opener of the store's files.

    expect(mentions(withOpener, "openImage")).not.toEqual(OPEN_IMAGE);
    // A name that only contains the word is not counted.
    expect(mentions([{ path: "x.ts", source: "requestDeletions(); reopenImage(); openImages();" }], "requestDeletion")).toEqual({});
    expect(mentions([{ path: "x.ts", source: "requestDeletions(); reopenImage(); openImages();" }], "openImage")).toEqual({});
  });
});

describe("module boundaries", () => {
  test("walks the real source tree", () => {

    const files: SourceFile[] = [

    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([

  });

  test("catches a deep import into the media module, post_media outside it, and the auth schema inside it", () => {

  test("catches auth pool and auth key references outside their owners", () => {
    const files: SourceFile[] = [
      { path: "routes/posts.ts", source: `const url = config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH;` },

      { path: "index.ts", source: `const k = config.AUTH_HMAC_KEY;` },

      { path: "moderation/intake.ts", source: `const key = deps.config.NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY;` },
      // The keys a key replaced are guarded as the key is: a contact is never encrypted again, so after a rotation they are

      { path: "moderation/context.ts", source: `const older = config.NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS;` },
      { path: "staff/routes.ts", source: `const older = config.TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS;` },

      { path: "lib/names.ts", source: `const MY_NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY_NAME = 1; const NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS = 2; const TOTP_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUSLY = 3;` },

      { path: "auth/context.ts", source: `notifierKey: parseVersionedKey(config.NOTIFIER_ENC_KEY), notifierPreviousKeys: config.NOTIFIER_ENC_KEYS_PREVIOUS.map(parseVersionedKey),` },
      // The staff command line may open the auth pool; another command line, or the staff module itself, may not.
      { path: "cli/other.ts", source: `const authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH);` },
      { path: "staff/audit.ts", source: `export function readKeys(authDb: Db) {}` },

  test("catches auth-schema imports inside the staff module", () => {

  test("catches the auth module's repository or session store inside the staff module, however it is imported", () => {

      { path: "staff/flows/y.ts", source: `const { createSessions } = await import("../../auth");` },

    ];
    expect(findViolations(files, new Set(), new Set())).toEqual([

  test("catches the moderation module reaching into another module, naming post_media, or opening the auth pool", () => {

  test("catches auth-schema imports inside the moderation module, and the auth module's repository or session store", () => {
```
