```ts
      const { key } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      const now = new Date();
      await authDb.update(staffKeys).set({ counter: 7, lastUsedAt: now }).where(eq(staffKeys.id, key.id));
      await authDb.update(staffKeys).set({ suspectAt: now, revokedAt: now }).where(eq(staffKeys.id, key.id));
      expect(await keyRow(key.id)).toMatchObject({ counter: 7, lastUsedAt: now, revokedAt: now, suspectAt: now });
    });

    test("a set revoked_at or suspect_at is never cleared or changed, and a key is never suspect without being revoked", async () => {
      const { key } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      const where = sql`where id = ${key.id}::uuid`;
      expect((await asAuth(sql`update auth.staff_keys set suspect_at = now() ${where}`))?.message).toMatch(/staff_keys_suspect_is_revoked/);
      expect(await asAuth(sql`update auth.staff_keys set revoked_at = now() ${where}`)).toBeNull();
      const revoked = await keyRow(key.id);
      for (const statement of [
        sql`update auth.staff_keys set revoked_at = null ${where}`,
        sql`update auth.staff_keys set revoked_at = revoked_at + interval '1 second' ${where}`,
      ]) {
        expect((await asAuth(statement))?.message).toMatch(/revoked_at is never cleared or changed/);
      }
      expect(await asAuth(sql`update auth.staff_keys set suspect_at = now() ${where}`)).toBeNull();
      for (const statement of [sql`update auth.staff_keys set suspect_at = null ${where}`, sql`update auth.staff_keys set suspect_at = suspect_at - interval '1 hour' ${where}`]) {
        expect((await asAuth(statement))?.message).toMatch(/suspect_at is never cleared or changed/);
      }
      // Unchanged values pass, so a revocation that repeats itself leaves the time it first recorded.
      expect(await asAuth(sql`update auth.staff_keys set revoked_at = coalesce(revoked_at, now()), counter = counter + 1 ${where}`)).toBeNull();
      expect((await keyRow(key.id)).revokedAt).toEqual(revoked.revokedAt);
    });

    test("it reads and deletes enrolments, and changes none of them", async () => {
      const { user } = await newStaffAccount(authDb, repo);
      const open = await issueEnrolment(migrateDb, user.id);
      for (const statement of [
        sql`update auth.staff_enrollments set used_at = now() where id = ${open.id}::uuid`,
        sql`update auth.staff_enrollments set expires_at = now() + interval '1 year' where id = ${open.id}::uuid`,
      ]) {
        expect((await asAuth(statement))?.message).toMatch(/permission denied for table staff_enrollments/);
      }
      expect(await authDb.select({ id: staffEnrollments.id }).from(staffEnrollments).where(eq(staffEnrollments.id, open.id))).toEqual([{ id: open.id }]);
      await authDb.delete(staffEnrollments).where(eq(staffEnrollments.id, open.id));
      expect(await migrateDb.$count(staffEnrollments, eq(staffEnrollments.id, open.id))).toBe(0);
    });

    test("a set used_at is never cleared or changed, even by the migrator that owns the table", async () => {
      const { enrolment } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      await rolledBack(migrateDb, async (tx) => {
        const err = await pgError(tx.transaction((sp) => sp.execute(sql`update auth.staff_enrollments set used_at = null where id = ${enrolment.id}::uuid`)));
        expect(err?.message).toMatch(/used_at is never cleared or changed/);
      });
      expect((await enrolmentRow(enrolment.id)).usedAt).toBeInstanceOf(Date);
    });
  });

  describe("staff sessions", () => {
    const session = (userId: string, keyId: string, created: Date, idleMs: number, absoluteMs: number) => ({
      id: sha256Hex(randomToken()),
      userId,
      keyId,
      createdAt: created,
      lastUsedAt: created,
      idleExpiresAt: new Date(created.getTime() + idleMs),
      absoluteExpiresAt: new Date(created.getTime() + absoluteMs),
      browser: "Firefox on Linux",
    });

    test("a session opened with the account's own key, for at most 12 hours, is stored with a random handle", async () => {
      const { user, key } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      const [row] = await authDb.insert(staffSessions).values(session(user.id, key.id, new Date(), 15 * 60_000, 12 * HOUR)).returning();
      expect(row!.handle).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
      expect(row).toMatchObject({ userId: user.id, keyId: key.id, revokedAt: null, browser: "Firefox on Linux" });
    });

    test("a session lasting beyond 12 hours, or idle past its absolute end, is refused", async () => {
      const { user, key } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      for (const [label, values] of [
        ["12 hours and 1 ms", session(user.id, key.id, new Date(), 15 * 60_000, 12 * HOUR + 1)],
        ["idle past the absolute end", session(user.id, key.id, new Date(), 2 * HOUR, HOUR)],
      ] as const) {
        const err = await pgError(authDb.insert(staffSessions).values(values));
        expect(err, label).toMatchObject({ code: "23514", message: expect.stringMatching(/staff_sessions_lifetime/) });
      }
    });

    test("a session pairing an account with another account's key is refused", async () => {
      const owner = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      const other = await newStaffAccount(authDb, repo);
      const err = await pgError(authDb.insert(staffSessions).values(session(other.user.id, owner.key.id, new Date(), 15 * 60_000, 12 * HOUR)));
      expect(err).toMatchObject({ code: "23503", message: expect.stringMatching(/staff_sessions_key_user_fk/) });
    });
  });

  describe("auth.forget_staff_keys", () => {
    test("changes nothing for a live account", async () => {
      const { user, key } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      const before = await keyRow(key.id);
      const [result] = await authDb.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select auth.forget_staff_keys(${user.id}::uuid) as n`);
      expect(result!.n).toBe(0);
      expect(await keyRow(key.id)).toEqual(before);
    });

    test("blanks a deleted account's revoked key names, AAGUIDs and transports, keeping what audit-verify needs", async () => {
      const { user, key } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      await addStaffKey(authDb, (await issueEnrolment(migrateDb, user.id)).token);
      // As the take-down leaves them before it calls the function: the account marked deleted, every key revoked.
      const revokedAt = new Date();
      await authDb.update(staffKeys).set({ revokedAt }).where(eq(staffKeys.userId, user.id));
      const before = await keyRow(key.id);
      await authDb.update(users).set({ deletedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(users.id, user.id));
      const [result] = await authDb.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select auth.forget_staff_keys(${user.id}::uuid) as n`);
      expect(result!.n).toBe(2);
      expect(await keyRow(key.id)).toEqual({ ...before, name: "", aaguid: null, transports: [] });
    });

    test("never blanks a live key, even when the auth role marks the account deleted around the call", async () => {
      // The auth role may set deleted_at, so the account's mark alone cannot guard the keys the column grants keep it
      // from changing; a key it has not revoked (which it can never undo) is never blanked. It can no longer clear the
      // mark (migration 0018, users_deleted_mark), so the transaction that set it is rolled back instead.
      const { user, key } = await newStaffKey(authDb, migrateDb, repo);
      const before = await keyRow(key.id);
      let forgotten = -1;
      await rolledBack(authDb, async (tx) => {
        await tx.update(users).set({ deletedAt: new Date() }).where(eq(users.id, user.id));
        const [result] = await tx.execute<{ n: number }>(sql`select auth.forget_staff_keys(${user.id}::uuid) as n`);
        forgotten = result!.n;
      });
      expect(forgotten).toBe(0);
      expect(await keyRow(key.id)).toEqual(before);
      expect((await repo.findUserById(user.id))!.deletedAt).toBeNull();
    });
  });

  describe("auth.append_audit", () => {
    test("writes each of the auth side's actions, in the caller's transaction", async () => {
      const start = await head();
      await rolledBack(authDb, async (tx) => {
        for (const [i, action] of AUTH_SIDE_ACTIONS.entries()) {
          const [row] = await tx.execute<{ place: number }>(
            sql`select auth.append_audit(${randomUUID()}::uuid, ${action}, 'staff_session', ${randomUUID()}, '{"via":"test"}'::jsonb, null, null, null, null, 'req-1')::int as place`,
          );
          expect(row!.place, action).toBe(start.seq + i + 1);
        }
        // A confirmed action carries its hash, its assertion and the key.
        const stepUp = JSON.stringify({ authenticatorData: "AAAA", clientDataJSON: "BBBB", signature: "CCCC" });
        const [confirmed] = await tx.execute<{ place: number }>(
          sql`select auth.append_audit(${randomUUID()}::uuid, 'staff_session_revoked', 'staff_session', ${randomUUID()}, '{"params":{}}'::jsonb, ${randomUUID()}::uuid, ${randomUUID()}::uuid, ${"ab".repeat(32)}, ${stepUp}::jsonb, 'req-2')::int as place`,
        );
        expect(confirmed!.place).toBe(start.seq + AUTH_SIDE_ACTIONS.length + 1);
      });
      expect(await head()).toEqual(start);
    });

    test("stores every column it is given, and an absent metadata as an empty object", async () => {
      const actorId = randomUUID();
      const staffSession = randomUUID();
      const keyId = randomUUID();
      const [written] = await withLockTimeout(authDb, (tx) =>
        tx.execute<{ place: number }>(
          sql`select auth.append_audit(${actorId}::uuid, 'staff_signed_out', 'staff_session', ${staffSession}, null, ${staffSession}::uuid, ${keyId}::uuid, null, null, 'req-signout')::int as place`,
        ),
      );
      const [row] = await apiDb.select().from(auditLog).where(eq(auditLog.chainSeq, written!.place));
      expect(row).toMatchObject({ actorId, action: "staff_signed_out", targetType: "staff_session", targetId: staffSession, metadata: {}, staffSession, keyId, actionHash: null, stepUp: null, requestId: "req-signout", chainVersion: 1 });
    });

    test("refuses every action outside its list, and writes nothing", async () => {
      const start = await head();
      for (const action of ["staff_key_added", "staff_enrollment_issued", "case_decided", "role_granted ", "", null]) {
        const err = await asAuth(sql`select auth.append_audit(${randomUUID()}::uuid, ${action}::text, null, null, '{}'::jsonb, null, null, null, null, null)`);
        expect(err?.message, String(action)).toMatch(/^auth\.append_audit does not write the action /);
      }
      expect(await head()).toEqual(start);
    });

    test("does not write a step-up without its key, as the table's check refuses", async () => {
      const stepUp = JSON.stringify({ authenticatorData: "AAAA", clientDataJSON: "BBBB", signature: "CCCC" });
      const err = await asAuth(sql`select auth.append_audit(${randomUUID()}::uuid, 'staff_session_revoked', null, null, '{}'::jsonb, null, null, ${"ab".repeat(32)}, ${stepUp}::jsonb, null)`);
      expect(err).toMatchObject({ code: "23514", message: expect.stringMatching(/audit_log_step_up_complete/) });
    });
  });

  test("the migrator owns every staff and chain function, pins its search path, and grants EXECUTE to the auth role alone", async () => {
    const rows = await apiDb.execute<{ name: string; owner: string; definer: boolean; config: string[] | null; api: boolean; auth: boolean }>(sql`
      select p.pronamespace::regnamespace::text || '.' || p.proname as name, p.proowner::regrole::text as owner, p.prosecdef as definer,
             p.proconfig as config, has_function_privilege('korbat_api', p.oid, 'execute') as api,
             has_function_privilege('korbat_auth', p.oid, 'execute') as auth
        from pg_proc p
       where (p.pronamespace = 'auth'::regnamespace and p.proname in ('add_staff_key', 'append_audit', 'forget_staff_keys', 'staff_never_cleared'))
          or (p.pronamespace = 'public'::regnamespace and p.proname in ('audit_chain', 'audit_chain_text'))
       order by 1`);
    const auth = ["search_path=auth, pg_temp"];
    const pub = ["search_path=public, pg_temp"];
    expect(rows.map((r) => ({ ...r }))).toEqual([
      { name: "auth.add_staff_key", owner: "korbat_migrate", definer: true, config: auth, api: false, auth: true },
      { name: "auth.append_audit", owner: "korbat_migrate", definer: true, config: auth, api: false, auth: true },
      { name: "auth.forget_staff_keys", owner: "korbat_migrate", definer: true, config: auth, api: false, auth: true },
      // A trigger function: it fires whoever writes the row, and nobody calls it.
      { name: "auth.staff_never_cleared", owner: "korbat_migrate", definer: false, config: auth, api: false, auth: false },
      { name: "public.audit_chain", owner: "korbat_migrate", definer: true, config: pub, api: false, auth: false },
      { name: "public.audit_chain_text", owner: "korbat_migrate", definer: false, config: pub, api: false, auth: false },
    ]);
  });
});
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/lab/README.md` (whole file)

```markdown
# The contention lab of moderation decisions

`contention.lab.ts` measures what a decision's transaction costs and what it meets (3c design, sections 2 and 12),
against the test database with migration 0016. The design names no place for it; it lives here.

It is a database lab. It issues its statements itself, as SQL: a decision is the lock on its subject's profile row, its
row in `decisions` and its rows in `decision_actions`, whose triggers do the rest; a like, a follow, the author's
deletion and the purge are the statements the social and media repositories issue; the purge's delete is the ordered
delete by owner (`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = $1 order by id for
update) returning id`). An intake is the moderation module's `recordIntake`. It uses no code of a later task.

Every measured transaction is rolled back, so the lab leaves no decision, and writes no audit row but one: the R4
removal that the redaction's rounds need committed (the last section) is a real, confirmed decision. The accounts it commits
(the large ones, written in bulk by the migrator, and the pair for the two-session rounds) are removed when it ends.

## Running it

From `apps/api`, with the scratch stack's data services up and the test database migrated:

    node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.lab.config.ts

No suite includes it (its file ends in `.lab.ts`). It takes three to four minutes. Each measurement is one line of JSON
in `.data/lab-contention.jsonl` at the repository's root (or the file `LAB_OUT` names), with `busyPercent`: the share of
processor time, over all cores, that was not idle in the second and a half before the measurement.

## The numbers of 2026-10-04, first run: a saturated machine

PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container on a Windows machine shared with other work. The machine was saturated
throughout: `busyPercent` read 94 to 99 before every measurement, most of it other projects' containers. These numbers
are upper bounds for this hardware; the second run below, on a quieter machine, is the one the design asks for.

### An account's seal (one session; one image on each post)

| image posts | busy | decision row | seal taken while deciding | answer that ends it | seal for good | lifting it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 97% | 104 ms | 180 ms | 254 ms | 282 ms | 232 ms |
| 5,000 | 99% | 18 ms | 1,123 ms | 1,057 ms | 1,131 ms | 995 ms |

- The seal taken while deciding locks the account's image rows in id order, writes one row of `seal_posts` for each post
  and writes every image row once. At 5,000 image posts the decision and its seal take 1.1 s, 0.19% of the ten minutes a
  step-up challenge lives.
- The seal for good that follows writes every image row twice in one transaction: the answer ends the first seal (each
  row back to visible, 1.06 s at 5,000), and the new seal seals each again (1.13 s). Lifting it is a fourth write (1.0 s).
- No post row is locked by any of them.

### The purge of an account (one session)

| image rows | frozen | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | 99% | 436 ms | 2,228 ms | 5,000 | 2.7 s |
| 5,000 | yes | 98% | 390 ms | 1,862 ms | 0 | 2.3 s |
| 20,000 | no | 94% | 1,471 ms | 6,090 ms | 20,000 | 7.6 s |
| 20,000 | yes | 97% | 1,724 ms | 5,821 ms | 0 | 7.6 s |

- The keep trigger reads the freeze once for each row: about 0.3 to 0.45 ms a row under this load, whether the row is
  then kept or deleted. The research lab's figures under load were 2 to 4 s at 5,000 rows and 7 to 16 s at 20,000; these
  lie at their lower end.
- "Frozen" is an unanswered report of child sexual abuse material about the account: every row is kept, and the delete
  answers none.

### A decision against everything else (two sessions, 40 rounds a pair, each side first in half of them)

Three decisions (an interim withhold of a post; a final removal that closes the post's case; a seal on the author's
account's case followed in the same transaction by the answer that ends it) against six other transactions (a like of
the post; a follow of the author; the author's deletion of the post; the author's purge; a notice of child sexual abuse
material that names the post and its author's account; a report of the post under a rule). Each side holds its locks for
15 ms before it rolls back. `busyPercent` was 96.

| decision | against | both completed | deadlocks | lock timeouts | longest transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| interim withhold | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 236 ms |
| interim withhold | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 116 ms |
| interim withhold | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 158 ms |
| interim withhold | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 232 ms |
| interim withhold | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 409 ms |
| interim withhold | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 318 ms |
| closing removal | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 183 ms |
| closing removal | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 145 ms |
| closing removal | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 194 ms |
| closing removal | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 171 ms |
| closing removal | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 207 ms |
| closing removal | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 231 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | like | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 254 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | follow | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 210 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | author's deletion | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 233 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | purge | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 419 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | notice naming post and account | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 264 ms |
| account's seal and its answer | report under a rule | 40 of 40 | 0 | 0 | 206 ms |

- 720 rounds, no deadlock and no lock timeout. The purge met none here either: the deadlock the design expects of it is
  with an intake that locks the account's image rows, which the intake does not do before Task 3.
- What makes this hold: a decision takes its subject's profile row first, as the author's deletion and the purge do; a
  like and a follow take that row in a mode a decision's does not conflict with; a seal locks image rows only; and an
  intake takes its cases in one order and each post's row only to read it.
- A finding the lab led to, now a test (`moderation-races.test.ts`): a report that arrives while a decision is closing
  its target's case waits where it opens a case (`insert into cases ... on conflict do nothing` waits for the transaction
  that is changing the conflicting row), and then opens a new case without a retry. The retry on `case_closed` is needed
  only when the decision has locked the case and not yet closed it when the report reads it.

## The numbers of 2026-10-04, second run: the final migration, a quieter machine

Run again after the review added a second deferred check to 0016 (queued by every row of the ledger, it runs at COMMIT,
which the lab's rolled-back transactions never reach). `busyPercent` read 17 to 28.

| image posts | busy | decision row | seal taken while deciding | answer that ends it | seal for good | lifting it |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 19% | 35 ms | 70 ms | 115 ms | 110 ms | 107 ms |
| 5,000 | 17% | 7 ms | 420 ms | 463 ms | 503 ms | 465 ms |

At 5,000 image posts the seal taken while deciding takes 0.43 s with its decision, 0.07% of the challenge's ten minutes;
the seal for good that follows it writes every image row twice in under a second.

| image rows | frozen | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | 28% | 182 ms | 888 ms | 5,000 | 1.1 s |
| 5,000 | yes | 24% | 108 ms | 791 ms | 0 | 0.9 s |
| 20,000 | no | 22% | 680 ms | 2,488 ms | 20,000 | 3.2 s |
| 20,000 | yes | 27% | 576 ms | 2,366 ms | 0 | 2.9 s |

The keep trigger costs about 0.12 to 0.18 ms a row here.

The two-session rounds at 24% busy: the same 18 pairs of 40 rounds each, every transaction completed, no deadlock and no
lock timeout, the longest transaction 124 ms.

# The lab of the intake's lock statement

`hold.lab.ts` measures what an intake's hold costs and what it meets (3c design, sections 5 and 12, Task 3), at the
repository: `MediaForCases.hold` with an owner pair, which is the statement that locks every image row on an account's
posts when a report of child sexual abuse material names the account
(`select ... from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id where m.post_id = any($1) or m.owner_id = any($2) order
by m.id for key share of m`). It also times the disposal's two statements over the same accounts, and runs the purge
against a notice about a post that quotes its author's own post. It runs against the test database with migration 0016,
through the media repository and the moderation module's own `recordIntake`; the purge is the social repository's
`purgeProfile` with the media repository's `purgeOwner` as its last act. Every measured transaction is rolled back; the
accounts it commits are removed when it ends.

    node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config vitest.lab.config.ts test/lab/hold.lab.ts

It takes about a minute and a quarter. Each measurement is one line of JSON in `.data/lab-hold.jsonl` (or the file
`LAB_OUT` names), with `busyPercent` as above. `LAB_ROUNDS` sets how many rounds the two sessions meet by chance (40
unless said).

## The numbers of 2026-10-04

Three runs on the shared Windows machine, PostgreSQL 18 in the scratch stack's container: two before the review of
Task 3 and one after its fixes. The machine was never quiet, most of the load other projects' containers:
`busyPercent` read 14 to 40 before the lock statement's runs of the first run (up to 100 before its last measurements),
14 to 83 before those of the second and 15 to 40 throughout the third. The times are upper bounds.

### The lock statement (`hold` with one owner pair; one image on each post; three runs each, a transaction of its own each)

| attached rows | run | busy | lock statement | WAL written |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | first | 29 to 40% | 36, 25 and 21 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 5,000 | second | 64 to 83% | 90, 65 and 26 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 5,000 | third | 23 to 31% | 46, 31 and 28 ms | 288, 274 and 274 kB |
| 20,000 | first | 14 to 19% | 114, 80 and 69 ms | 1,153, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |
| 20,000 | second | 14 to 76% | 102, 180 and 198 ms | 1,408, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |
| 20,000 | third | 23 to 31% | 151, 123 and 102 ms | 1,153, 1,097 and 1,097 kB |

- The research lab's figures (`lab-gate-k`, H) were 77 ms and 287 kB at 5,000 rows and 102 ms and 1.1 MB at 20,000:
  these agree. The lock writes its mark to each row it takes, though no column changes: about 55 bytes of WAL a row.
- The plan is LockRows over a Sort on `m.id` over a hash join of `post_media` and `posts`, as the design says of the
  owner form. In the test database the lab's account owns most image rows, so `post_media` is scanned whole; the sort
  took 0.6 MB of memory at 5,000 rows and 2.5 MB at 20,000.
- A whole notice on the path for child sexual abuse material that names the account (its rows, the copy of the profile,
  the hold and the snapshot) took 72, 95 and 77 ms at 5,000 rows and 104, 238 and 147 ms at 20,000; one that names a
  post of the account as well took 85, 91 and 80 ms at 5,000 and 743 (at 90% busy), 299 and 147 ms at 20,000.
- The purge's ordered delete (`purgeOwner`) right after such a notice, in the same transaction, deleted no row: 1.4,
  1.6 and 1.3 s at 5,000 rows, 5.6 and 5.5 s (73 to 100% busy) and 3.2 s (31% busy) at 20,000, the keep trigger reading
  the freeze once for each row.

### The disposal's two statements (one batch of `dropDisposable`, and `overdueDeletions`)

The account's rows are all attached. In the first two lines nothing of the account is disposable: its posts are
visible. In the last, the account is reported on the path for child sexual abuse material and every post of it is
deleted, so every row carries a mark of disposal and none may go.

| what | attached rows | busy | `dropDisposable` | `overdueDeletions` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nothing disposable, the freeze a condition of its own (as first built) | 5,000 | 100% | 3,332 ms | 3,332 ms |
| | 20,000 | 97% | 14,226 ms | 13,863 ms |
| nothing disposable, the marks tested first (as built now) | 5,000 | 24% | 18 ms | 8 ms |
| | 20,000 | 40% | 62 ms | 19 ms |
| every row marked and frozen (as built now) | 5,000 | 18% | 1,285 ms | 1,174 ms |
| | 20,000 | 26% | 4,148 ms | 3,666 ms |

- As first built, the predicate was `... and (marks) and (m.post_id is null or not public.post_frozen(m.post_id))`.
  The second condition names `post_media` alone, so the planner made it the filter of that table's scan and called the
  freeze for every attached image row in the table before a mark was tested. The review measured 0.9 s at 5,000 rows
  and 3.4 s at 20,000 on a quieter machine; the first two lines are the same statement on a saturated one.
- Now the marks and the freeze are one condition, `case when (marks) then (m.post_id is null or not
  public.post_frozen(m.post_id)) else false end`: it names all three tables, so it runs where they are joined, and the
  freeze is read only for a row that carries a mark. `media-cases.test.ts` pins that no scan's filter names the
  predicate, under the planner's own plan and under each join method alone.
- What remains is the last pair of lines: a frozen account whose posts are all deleted (a purged account under an
  unanswered report, or under a seal for good) costs one read of the freeze for each kept row, about 0.2 ms, at every
  round of the disposal and at every count of overdue rows, for as long as the freeze lasts.

### The purge against a notice about a post that quotes its author's own post

A report of child sexual abuse material about a post that quotes another is taken in as two items, so a notice about a
post that quotes its author's own post holds two posts of one account for share, in id order, while the purge writes
both. The lab's account has such a pair, four images on each post; the notice names the quoting post and the account.
The notice's side counts the runs the moderation module made, so a deadlock it absorbed by running again shows; nothing
runs a purge again, so a deadlock that picks the purge shows as its error.

By chance (two sessions, each side first in half the rounds, a few milliseconds ahead, each holding its locks for
15 ms before it rolls back):

| purge | rounds | busy | purge | notice | deadlocks | longest transaction |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| as first built (counters, then the posts in id order) | 200 | 95% | 200 of 200 | 200 of 200, each in one run | 0 | 528 ms |
| as built now (every post locked first, in id order) | 40 | 25% | 40 of 40 | 40 of 40, each in one run | 0 | 139 ms |

Staged (ten rounds a shape: the notice has copied the first of the two posts and is held there, the purge comes to
wait, the notice goes on to the second post):

| purge | the quoting post has the lower id | the quoted post has the lower id and was deleted by its author |
|---|---|---|
| as first built: the counters of what its posts quote, then the posts in id order | 10 of 10: the purge ends with 40P01 | not run |
| the account's posts that are not deleted locked first, in id order | 10 of 10: both complete | 10 of 10: the purge ends with 40P01 |
| every post of the account locked first, in id order (as built now) | 10 of 10: both complete | 10 of 10: both complete |

- As first built, the purge's quote counter wrote the quoted post before the ordered statement asked for the quoting
  one, which the notice held: each waited for the other. The window is one statement of the notice wide, so 200 rounds
  by chance never met it, and every staged round did. PostgreSQL ended the purge each time: a session looks for a
  deadlock once it has waited a second, and the purge was the first to wait. The notice went through in one run. A purge
  that ends this way is finished by the purge job within five minutes.
- Locking only the posts that are not deleted leaves the same wait in the second shape: a live post that quotes (or
  replies to) its author's own deleted post has that post's counter written by the purge, and a report of child sexual
  abuse material holds a deleted post like any other. So the purge locks every post of the account first.
- What stays unordered: the counters of other accounts' posts that the purged account replied to, quoted, liked or
  reposted, which the purge writes after its own posts; and the author's deletion of one post, which writes the post
  and then the post it replied to or quoted.
- Before the review this pair ran with two plain posts (and with the purge as first built): 40 of 40 on both sides in
  both runs, no deadlock, the longest transaction 307 ms at 64% busy and 200 ms at 23%.
- What the two-session tests add (`media-cases.test.ts`): when the notice locks first, the purge waits and then keeps
  every attached row; when the purge deletes first, the notice waits, locks nothing and is stored without an error.

### The contention lab again

`contention.lab.ts` issues the purge's statements as the repositories issue them since Task 3: every post of the
account locked in id order (`select id from posts where author_id = $1 order by id for update`), then the tombstones,
and the ordered delete of the image rows last. Three runs on 2026-10-04 with the intake locking image rows and placing
its holds. The first, before the review, still tombstoned by one ordered statement and met a machine at 9 to 14% busy
(53 and 93 before the two purges of 20,000 rows). The second and the third issue the statements above: the second met
a saturated machine (93 to 100% throughout), so its times say more about the machine than about the change; the third
a quiet one (6 to 16%). "Tombstones" is the lock statement and the update together.

| image rows | frozen | run | busy | tombstones | ordered delete | rows deleted | whole purge |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5,000 | no | first | 9% | 170 ms | 891 ms | 5,000 | 1.1 s |
| 5,000 | yes | first | 14% | 120 ms | 827 ms | 0 | 1.0 s |
| 20,000 | no | first | 53% | 603 ms | 4,019 ms | 20,000 | 4.6 s |
| 20,000 | yes | first | 93% | 1,440 ms | 4,249 ms | 0 | 5.7 s |
| 5,000 | no | second | 100% | 481 ms | 3,136 ms | 5,000 | 3.6 s |
| 5,000 | yes | second | 100% | 309 ms | 3,423 ms | 0 | 3.8 s |
| 20,000 | no | second | 100% | 1,934 ms | 8,112 ms | 20,000 | 10.1 s |
| 20,000 | yes | second | 100% | 2,249 ms | 8,467 ms | 0 | 10.7 s |
| 5,000 | no | third | 16% | 91 ms | 827 ms | 5,000 | 0.9 s |
| 5,000 | yes | third | 6% | 103 ms | 730 ms | 0 | 0.8 s |
| 20,000 | no | third | 13% | 442 ms | 2,207 ms | 20,000 | 2.7 s |
| 20,000 | yes | third | 13% | 481 ms | 1,977 ms | 0 | 2.5 s |

Locking the posts first costs nothing that shows: at 5,000 posts the lock statement and the update together took 91
and 103 ms, where the one ordered statement took 170 and 120 ms.

The 18 pairs of 40 rounds: in every run each transaction completed, with no deadlock and no lock timeout; the longest
transaction was 137 ms in the first (12% busy), 562 ms in the second (100% busy) and 116 ms in the third (13% busy).
The account's seal taken while deciding: 84 ms at 1,000 image posts and 2.2 s at 5,000 in the first run (13% busy; 0.4
and 1.1 s in Task 2's runs), 361 ms and 3.3 s in the second, 58 and 156 ms in the third.

### What the lab's tests found

- **A batch that was not one.** `dropDisposable` as the design writes it (`delete from post_media where id in (select
  ... order by id limit $1 for update)`) can delete more than its limit. When the planner joins the delete's rows to
  the sub-select by a nested loop, the sub-select runs again for every row; each run skips the rows this statement has
  deleted already and lets the next ones in. On a fresh test database one call deleted all 60 disposable rows under a
  limit of 25, and with hash joins, merge joins, materialising, hashed aggregation and sorting switched off it deleted
  33 of 36. The repository therefore chooses the batch in a materialized common table expression, which runs once
  whatever the plan (`with batch as materialized (select ... order by m.id limit $1 for update of m) delete from
  post_media where id in (select id from batch) returning id`); `media-cases.test.ts` holds the bound under those
  planner settings. The ordered deletes of the author's deletion and the purge have no limit, so the same re-run changes
  nothing they delete.
- **The freeze read for every row.** The disposal's two statements, above.
- **The purge and its own posts.** The staged rounds, above.

## The numbers of 2026-10-09: the R4 redaction (migration 0018)

`contention.lab.ts` gains one test for `redact_r4_body` (3c design, sections 2 and 6.4): the redaction takes its
decision's case, then the post, then the post's images in id order, the order of `moderation_apply` and of an intake's
locks, and the design asks for it to be measured against both. The post has four images. Its R4 removal is the one
thing this lab confirms with a real staff key (the software authenticator, as `decideForTest` does), because a
redaction acts only on a committed decision; it is dated back seven months, so that it is final for its author. The
redaction itself, and everything that runs against it, is rolled back in every round, so each round finds the decision
due again. The removal's case goes with the lab's accounts at the end; its one audit row stays, as every real
decision's does. Run alone with `-t "the R4 redaction"`.

Two runs: the test alone on a machine busy with other work (`busyPercent` 82), then the whole file on a quieter one
(`busyPercent` 22; the whole file took 122 s).

| the redaction against | rounds | redaction | other side | longest transaction, busy | longest, quieter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (alone, one session) | 1 | ok | | 67 ms | 29 ms |
| an interim withhold on the post's other, open case, whose trigger runs `moderation_apply` on the post | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 233 ms | 68 ms |
| a report under a rule, which locks the post `FOR SHARE` and holds its images | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 125 ms | 104 ms |
| a notice of child sexual abuse material naming the post and its author's account, which locks the images through both | 40 | 40 ok | 40 ok | 123 ms | 83 ms |

- No deadlock and no refusal in 120 rounds of either run, each side first in half of them. The redaction and a decision on the post's
  other case meet at the post's row, which both take `FOR UPDATE` before any image row; the redaction and a report meet
  there too (`FOR UPDATE` against `FOR SHARE`); a notice that reaches the images through the account takes them
  `FOR KEY SHARE`, which the redaction's `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` does not wait for.
- That last pair is the one the design accepts as a race and not as a wait (6.4): a report about the author's account
  that commits between the redaction's check of the freeze and its erasure of the snapshots leaves the body blank, the
  snapshots kept and the decision unmarked, and the round after the answer finishes it. The database test of
  `redact_r4_body` stages exactly that.
```

### Replace `apps/api/test/lab/contention.lab.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import { randomBytes, randomUUID } from "node:crypto";
import { appendFileSync, mkdirSync } from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, test } from "vitest";
import type { CaseDecidedParams } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { closeDb, createDb, type Db, type DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { createAuthRepo } from "../../src/auth/repo";
import { loadConfig } from "../../src/config";
import { insertAction, insertDecision } from "../../src/moderation/repo";
import { deciderWorld, type DeciderWorld } from "../integration/moderation-decide";
import {
  aPost,
  act,
  anAccount,
  decisionParams,
  ground,
  intake,
  newImageRow,
  newPostRow,
  newTestStaff,
  raised,
  removeFixtures,
  report,
  staffProfile,
  type DecisionInput,
  type TestStaff,
} from "../integration/moderation-fixtures";
import { ageCase } from "../integration/retention-fixtures";
import { newProfile } from "../integration/social-fixtures";
import { rolledBack } from "../integration/staff-fixtures";

/**
 * The contention lab of moderation decisions (3c design, sections 2 and 12): what a decision's transaction costs and what
 * it meets, measured against the real database with migration 0016. The lab issues the statements itself, as SQL: a
 * decision is its profile lock, its row and its ledger rows, whose triggers do the rest; a like, a follow, a deletion and
 * a purge are the statements the social and media repositories issue. Every measured transaction is rolled back, so the
 * lab leaves no decision. Its one audit row is the R4 removal that the redaction's rounds need committed, which is a real,
 * confirmed decision. The accounts and posts it commits for the two-session rounds and the large accounts are removed at
 * the end. It writes one line of JSON for each measurement, with how busy the machine's
 * processors were just before it. Run it by hand (see README.md); no suite includes it.
 */

/** Where the measurements go, one line of JSON each: the file LAB_OUT names, or lab-contention.jsonl in the repository's .data folder (the lab runs from apps/api). */
const OUT = process.env.LAB_OUT ?? path.resolve(process.cwd(), "../../.data/lab-contention.jsonl");
function line(name: string, result: Record<string, unknown>): void {
  const text = JSON.stringify({ name, at: new Date().toISOString(), ...result });
  mkdirSync(path.dirname(OUT), { recursive: true });
  appendFileSync(OUT, text + String.fromCharCode(10));
  console.log(`LAB ${text}`);
}

/** The share of processor time that was not idle over this many milliseconds, across all cores: how loaded the machine is. */
async function busy(ms = 1500): Promise<number> {
  const read = () => os.cpus().reduce((sum, cpu) => ({ idle: sum.idle + cpu.times.idle, all: sum.all + cpu.times.user + cpu.times.nice + cpu.times.sys + cpu.times.irq + cpu.times.idle }), { idle: 0, all: 0 });
  const before = read();
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));
  const after = read();
  return Math.round((1 - (after.idle - before.idle) / Math.max(1, after.all - before.all)) * 100);
}

async function timed(fn: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<number> {
  const start = performance.now();
  await fn();
  return Math.round(performance.now() - start);
}

describe.skipIf(!process.env.INTEGRATION)("lab: the contention of moderation decisions", () => {
  let apiDb: Db;
  let authDb: Db;
  let migrateDb: Db;
  let mod: TestStaff;
  let admin: TestStaff;
  const committed: string[] = [];
  /** The one thing the lab confirms with a real key: the R4 removal that the redaction's rounds make final again and again. */
  let world: DeciderWorld | null = null;

  beforeAll(async () => {
    const config = loadConfig();
    apiDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_API, { max: 8 });
    authDb = createDb(config.DATABASE_URL_AUTH, { max: 2 });
    migrateDb = createDb(process.env.DATABASE_URL_MIGRATE!, { max: 2 });
    const repo = createAuthRepo(authDb);
    mod = await newTestStaff(authDb, migrateDb, repo, "moderator");
    admin = await newTestStaff(authDb, migrateDb, repo, "admin");
  });
  afterAll(async () => {
    await removeFixtures(migrateDb, committed);
    await world?.close();
    await Promise.all([closeDb(apiDb), closeDb(authDb), closeDb(migrateDb)]);
  });

  /** A committed account with this many posts of one image each, written in bulk by the migrator. */
  async function largeAccount(posts: number): Promise<{ id: string; handle: string }> {
    const [id, handle] = [randomUUID(), `lab_${randomBytes(5).toString("hex")}`];
    committed.push(id);
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into profiles (id, handle, display_name) values (${id}::uuid, ${handle}, 'Lab account')`);
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into posts (author_id, body, created_at) select ${id}::uuid, 'a lab post', now() - interval '40 days' from generate_series(1, ${posts}::int)`);
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`insert into post_media (owner_id, status, width, height, blurhash) select ${id}::uuid, 'ready', 1200, 800, 'L2Eo_P_3jb_3~qoL' from generate_series(1, ${posts}::int)`);
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`analyze posts`);
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`analyze post_media`);
    // Each image goes onto the post of the same rank. The two numbered sets are joined by a hash: on fresh rows the planner
    // otherwise pairs them in a nested loop, which at 20,000 rows is 400 million comparisons.
    await migrateDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
      await tx.execute(sql`set local enable_nestloop = off`);
      await tx.execute(sql`
        with p as materialized (select id, row_number() over (order by id) as n from posts where author_id = ${id}::uuid),
             i as materialized (select id, row_number() over (order by id) as n from post_media where owner_id = ${id}::uuid)
        update post_media m set post_id = p.id, position = 0, alt_text = 'a lab image' from p join i on i.n = p.n where m.id = i.id`);
    });
    await migrateDb.execute(sql`analyze post_media`);
    return { id, handle };
  }
  /**
   * One decision's statements inside `tx`, each timed: the subject's profile lock, the decision's row, each ledger row.
   * The params are built before, as the console builds them before it asks for the key: their texts are saved rows.
   */
  async function decisionWith(tx: DbTx, staff: TestStaff, subject: string, caseId: string, params: CaseDecidedParams) {
    const id = randomUUID();
    const lock = await timed(() => tx.execute(sql`select id from profiles where id = ${subject}::uuid for no key update`));
    const decision = await timed(() => insertDecision(tx, { id, caseId, decidedBy: staff.id, params }));
    const actions: number[] = [];
    for (const action of params.actions) actions.push(await timed(() => insertAction(tx, id, action)));
    return { id, lock, decision, actions };
  }
  /** The same, with the params built inside `tx`: for a single session, where nothing waits for what building them touches. */
  const decisionIn = async (tx: DbTx, staff: TestStaff, subject: string, caseId: string, input: DecisionInput) =>
    decisionWith(tx, staff, subject, caseId, await decisionParams(tx, staff, caseId, input));
  const withStaff = (fn: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<void>) =>
    rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
      await staffProfile(tx, mod);
      await staffProfile(tx, admin);
      await fn(tx);
    });

  test("an account's seal at 1,000 and at 5,000 image posts, and the seal for good that follows it", async () => {
    for (const posts of [1000, 5000]) {
      const owner = await largeAccount(posts);
      const load = await busy();
      await withStaff(async (tx) => {
        const { caseId } = await report(tx, anAccount(owner.id, owner.handle), "csam");
        // A seal taken while deciding: one statement locks the account's image rows in id order, one row of seal_posts for
        // each post, and every image row is written once.
        const interim = await decisionIn(tx, mod, owner.id, caseId, { kind: "interim", ruleId: "R2", actions: [act("seal_media")] });
        // The seal for good that answers the report: the answer ends the first seal (every image row written back), and
        // the second seal writes every row again.
        const final = await decisionIn(tx, admin, owner.id, caseId, { kind: "final", ruleId: "R2", actions: [act("seal_media")] });
        // And its lifting, a correction: every row written a fourth time.
        const lift = await decisionIn(tx, admin, owner.id, caseId, { kind: "correction", reviewsDecisionId: final.id, actions: [act("unseal_media")] });
        line("account seal", {
          posts,
          busyPercent: load,
          interimDecisionMs: interim.decision,
          interimSealMs: interim.actions[0],
          finalDecisionEndsInterimMs: final.decision,
          finalSealMs: final.actions[0],
          liftMs: lift.actions[0],
          challengeShare: `${(((interim.decision + interim.actions[0]!) / 600_000) * 100).toFixed(2)}% of ten minutes for the seal taken while deciding`,
        });
      });
    }
  });

  test("the purge of an account with 5,000 and with 20,000 image rows, free and frozen", async () => {
    for (const rows of [5000, 20000]) {
      const owner = await largeAccount(rows);
      for (const frozen of [false, true]) {
        const load = await busy();
        await withStaff(async (tx) => {
          if (frozen) await report(tx, anAccount(owner.id, owner.handle), "csam");
          const lock = await timed(() => tx.execute(sql`select handle from profiles where id = ${owner.id}::uuid for update`));
          // Every post of the account under a row lock, in id order, before any is written; then the tombstones. Both are
          // counted as "tombstones", as the one statement was that did both before.
          const tombstones = await timed(async () => {
            await tx.execute(sql`select id from posts where author_id = ${owner.id}::uuid order by id for update`);
            await tx.execute(sql`update posts set state = 'deleted_by_author', deleted_at = now(), body = '' where author_id = ${owner.id}::uuid and state <> 'deleted_by_author'`);
          });
          const profile = await timed(() => tx.execute(sql`update profiles set display_name = 'Deleted account', bio = '', deleted_at = now() where id = ${owner.id}::uuid and deleted_at is null`));
          let deleted = 0;
          // The ordered delete by owner, as the media repository issues it, last: the keep trigger reads the freeze once for each row.
          const images = await timed(async () => {
            deleted = (await tx.execute(sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = ${owner.id}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`)).length;
          });
          line("account purge", { imageRows: rows, frozen, busyPercent: load, profileLockMs: lock, tombstonesMs: tombstones, orderedDeleteMs: images, rowsDeleted: deleted, profileMs: profile, totalMs: lock + tombstones + images + profile });
        });
      }
    }
  });

  test("a decision against likes, follows, the author's deletion, the purge, an intake, an account's seal and a closing decision: forty rounds each, both orders", async () => {
    const [author, liker] = [await newProfile(apiDb), await newProfile(apiDb)];
    committed.push(author.id, liker.id);
    const postId = await newPostRow(apiDb, author.id);
    for (const position of [0, 1]) await newImageRow(apiDb, author.id, postId, position);
    // Committed once: the post's case under a rule, and its author's account's case on the path for child sexual abuse
    // material, with the staff profiles the decisions name. Every round's transactions roll back, so the cases never move.
    await staffProfile(apiDb, mod);
    await staffProfile(apiDb, admin);
    committed.push(mod.id, admin.id);
    const postCase = (await intake(apiDb, ground.rule(liker.id), aPost(postId))).items[0]!.caseId!;
    const accountCase = (await report(apiDb, anAccount(author.id, author.handle), "csam")).caseId;
    const pause = (tx: DbTx) => tx.execute(sql`select pg_sleep(0.015)`);
    // The params of each decision, built and their texts saved once: every decision here rolls back, so its case keeps its
    // version and its texts stay unconfirmed, and the same params decide again in the next round.
    const withhold = await decisionParams(apiDb, mod, postCase, { kind: "interim", actions: [act("withhold")] });
    const removal = await decisionParams(apiDb, mod, postCase, { kind: "final", actions: [act("remove")] });
    const seal = await decisionParams(apiDb, mod, accountCase, { kind: "interim", ruleId: "R2", actions: [act("seal_media")] });
    const answer = await decisionParams(apiDb, admin, accountCase, { kind: "final", outcome: "no_violation" });

    /** The decisions, each holding its locks for a moment before it rolls back. */
    const decisions: Record<string, (tx: DbTx) => Promise<unknown>> = {
      "interim withhold of the post": (tx) => decisionWith(tx, mod, author.id, postCase, withhold),
      "final removal that closes the post's case": (tx) => decisionWith(tx, mod, author.id, postCase, removal),
      "account's seal, then the answer that ends it": async (tx) => {
        await decisionWith(tx, mod, author.id, accountCase, seal);

        await decisionWith(tx, admin, author.id, accountCase, { ...answer, stateVersion: answer.stateVersion + 1 });
      },

    /** What runs against them, as the statements the repositories issue. */
    const others: Record<string, (tx: DbTx) => Promise<unknown>> = {
      like: async (tx) => {

        await tx.execute(sql`update posts set like_count = like_count + 1 where id = ${postId}::uuid`);

        await tx.execute(sql`update profiles set post_count = greatest(0, post_count - 1) where id = ${author.id}::uuid`);
      },
      // As the repositories issue it since the deleters take their rows in id order: every post of the account locked in id
      // order before any is written, then the tombstones, and the image rows last.
      purge: async (tx) => {
        await tx.execute(sql`select handle from profiles where id = ${author.id}::uuid for update`);
        await tx.execute(sql`select id from posts where author_id = ${author.id}::uuid order by id for update`);
        await tx.execute(sql`update posts set state = 'deleted_by_author', deleted_at = now(), body = '' where author_id = ${author.id}::uuid and state <> 'deleted_by_author'`);
        await tx.execute(sql`update profiles set display_name = 'Deleted account', bio = '', deleted_at = now() where id = ${author.id}::uuid and deleted_at is null`);
        await tx.execute(sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = ${author.id}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`);
      },
      "notice naming the post and its author's account": async (tx) => {
        await intake(tx, ground.csam(), [aPost(postId, 1), anAccount(author.id, author.handle, 2)]);
      },
      "report under a rule": async (tx) => {
        await intake(tx, ground.rule((await newProfile(tx as unknown as Db)).id), aPost(postId));

    const ROUNDS = 40;
    const load = await busy();
    for (const [decisionName, decision] of Object.entries(decisions)) {
      for (const [otherName, other] of Object.entries(others)) {
        const counts: Record<string, number> = {};
        let longest = 0;
        for (let round = 0; round < ROUNDS; round++) {
          const side = (fn: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<unknown>, delay: number) => async () => {
            await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay));
            const start = performance.now();
            const outcome = await rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
              await fn(tx);
              await pause(tx);

              () => "ok",
              (err: unknown) => {
                const fromDatabase = raised(err);

              },
            );
            longest = Math.max(longest, performance.now() - start);
            return outcome;
          };
          // Each side starts first in half the rounds, a few milliseconds ahead.
          const ahead = Math.floor(Math.random() * 8);
          const [a, b] = await Promise.all(round % 2 === 0 ? [side(decision, 0)(), side(other, ahead)()] : [side(decision, ahead)(), side(other, 0)()]);
          for (const [who, outcome] of [["decision", a], ["other", b]] as const) counts[`${who}: ${outcome}`] = (counts[`${who}: ${outcome}`] ?? 0) + 1;
        }
        line("contention", { decision: decisionName, against: otherName, rounds: ROUNDS, busyPercent: load, outcomes: counts, longestMs: Math.round(longest) });
      }
    }
  });

  test("the R4 redaction against a decision that derives the post's level, a report that holds the post's images and a notice that locks them through the account: forty rounds each, both orders", async () => {
    // Migration 0018's redaction takes its decision's case, then the post, then the post's images in id order, as
    // moderation_apply and an intake do. A committed R4 removal, final for its author seven months ago, is redacted in a
    // transaction that is rolled back, so every round finds it due again.
    world = deciderWorld(apiDb);
    const staff = await world.staff("moderator");
    const [author, reporter] = [await newProfile(apiDb), await newProfile(apiDb)];
    committed.push(author.id, reporter.id);
    const postId = await newPostRow(apiDb, author.id);
    for (const position of [0, 1, 2, 3]) await newImageRow(apiDb, author.id, postId, position);
    const r4Case = (await intake(apiDb, ground.rule(reporter.id), aPost(postId))).items[0]!.caseId!;
    const removal = await world.decideAs(staff, r4Case, { kind: "final", ruleId: "R4", actions: [act("remove")] });
    if (typeof removal === "string") throw new Error(`the lab's R4 removal was not recorded: ${removal}`);
    await ageCase(migrateDb, r4Case, "7 months");
    // A second, open case of the same post, on which the other side decides: its measure derives the post's level.
    const openCase = (await report(apiDb, aPost(postId))).caseId;
    const withhold = await decisionParams(apiDb, staff, openCase, { kind: "interim", actions: [act("withhold")] });
    const pause = (tx: DbTx) => tx.execute(sql`select pg_sleep(0.015)`);

    const redaction = async (tx: DbTx) => {
      const [row] = (await tx.execute(sql`select public.redact_r4_body(${removal.decisionId}::uuid) as done`)) as unknown as { done: boolean }[];
      if (!row!.done) throw new Error("the redaction changed nothing");
    };
    const others: Record<string, (tx: DbTx) => Promise<unknown>> = {
      "interim withhold on the post's other case (moderation_apply)": (tx) => decisionWith(tx, staff, author.id, openCase, withhold),
      "report under a rule, which holds the post's images": async (tx) => {
        await intake(tx, ground.rule((await newProfile(tx as unknown as Db)).id), aPost(postId));
      },
      "notice naming the post and its author's account, which locks the images through both": async (tx) => {
        await intake(tx, ground.csam(), [aPost(postId, 1), anAccount(author.id, author.handle, 2)]);
      },
    };

    const ROUNDS = 40;
    const load = await busy();
    const single = await timed(() => rolledBack(apiDb, redaction));
    line("redaction alone", { images: 4, busyPercent: load, ms: single });
    for (const [otherName, other] of Object.entries(others)) {
      const counts: Record<string, number> = {};
      let longest = 0;
      for (let round = 0; round < ROUNDS; round++) {
        const side = (fn: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<unknown>, delay: number) => async () => {
          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delay));
          const start = performance.now();
          const outcome = await rolledBack(apiDb, async (tx) => {
            await fn(tx);
            await pause(tx);
          }).then(
            () => "ok",
            (err: unknown) => {
              const fromDatabase = raised(err);
              return fromDatabase ? `${fromDatabase.code} ${fromDatabase.message}` : (err as { code?: string }).code ?? String(err);
            },
          );
          longest = Math.max(longest, performance.now() - start);
          return outcome;
        };
        // Each side starts first in half the rounds, a few milliseconds ahead.
        const ahead = Math.floor(Math.random() * 8);
        const [a, b] = await Promise.all(round % 2 === 0 ? [side(redaction, 0)(), side(other, ahead)()] : [side(redaction, ahead)(), side(other, 0)()]);
        for (const [who, outcome] of [["redaction", a], ["other", b]] as const) counts[`${who}: ${outcome}`] = (counts[`${who}: ${outcome}`] ?? 0) + 1;
      }
      line("redaction contention", { redaction: "redact_r4_body of a post removal", against: otherName, rounds: ROUNDS, busyPercent: load, outcomes: counts, longestMs: Math.round(longest) });
    }
  });
});
```

```ts
 * may send, what the console lists of the appeals that wait, and the marks by which the console says who may review one.
 */
const id = (n: number) => `00000000-0000-4000-8000-${String(n).padStart(12, "0")}`;
const TIME = "2026-10-04T10:00:00.000Z";
const TOKEN = "t".repeat(43);

describe("an appeal's and a re-examination's request", () => {
  test("the statement is optional and free of form, under the rules of every free text, and at most 2000 characters", () => {
    expect(STATEMENT_MAX).toBe(2000);
    expect(DAILY_LIMITS).toEqual({ appeals: 5, reexaminations: 5 });
    for (const schema of [AppealRequest, ReexamineRequest]) {
      expect(schema.parse({})).toEqual({});
      expect(schema.parse({ statement: "Line one.\nLine two." })).toEqual({ statement: "Line one.\nLine two." });
      expect(schema.safeParse({ statement: "x".repeat(STATEMENT_MAX) }).success).toBe(true);
      expect(schema.safeParse({ statement: "x".repeat(STATEMENT_MAX + 1) }).success).toBe(false);
      // Nothing is trimmed, changed or dropped: an empty text, a control character and an unknown member are refused.
      for (const statement of ["", "   ", `a${String.fromCharCode(0)}b`, `a${String.fromCharCode(0x202e)}b`]) expect(schema.safeParse({ statement }).success, JSON.stringify(statement)).toBe(false);
      expect(schema.safeParse({ statement: "x", decisionId: id(1) }).success).toBe(false);
      expect(schema.safeParse({ statement: 5 }).success).toBe(false);
    }
  });

  test("a notifier names the notice by its reference with a token, and the item by its position on the status page, 1 to 20", () => {
    const request = { ref: "N-ABCDEFGH23", token: TOKEN, position: 1 };
    expect(NoticeReexamineRequest.parse(request)).toEqual(request);
    expect(NoticeReexamineRequest.parse({ ...request, position: 20, statement: "Look again." })).toEqual({ ...request, position: 20, statement: "Look again." });
    for (const position of [0, 21, 1.5, "1"]) expect(NoticeReexamineRequest.safeParse({ ...request, position }).success, String(position)).toBe(false);
    for (const broken of [{ ...request, ref: "nope" }, { ...request, token: undefined }, { ...request, itemId: id(1) }, { ref: request.ref, position: 1 }]) {
      expect(NoticeReexamineRequest.safeParse(broken).success, JSON.stringify(broken)).toBe(false);
    }
  });

  test("the answer names the positions that are examined again: one, or two with the item korbat added for a quoted post", () => {
    expect(ReexamineResponse.parse({ positions: [1] })).toEqual({ positions: [1] });
    expect(ReexamineResponse.parse({ positions: [1, 11] })).toEqual({ positions: [1, 11] });
    for (const positions of [[], [1, 11, 2], [0], [21]]) expect(ReexamineResponse.safeParse({ positions }).success, JSON.stringify(positions)).toBe(false);
  });
});

      reveals: { total: 0, items: [] },

      findingsToday: [],
      mailsWaiting: { receipts: 0, authorMails: 0, outcomes: 0 },
      mailsFailed: { receipts: 0, authorMails: 0, outcomes: 0 },
      releaseOverdue: 0,
      erasureOverdue: { caseEvidence: 0, intakeRecords: 0, statements: 0, redactions: 0, images: 0, drafts: 0, accessLog: 0, contacts: 0 },
      deferUnproven: false,
      protectionLifted: { total: 0, items: [] },
      sealsDeclined: { total: 0, items: [] },

    expect(StaffOverview.parse(overview)).toEqual(overview);

});

describe("the review's request", () => {
  const params = {
    stateVersion: 2,
    appealId: id(1),
    snapshotId: id(2),
    snapshotDigest: "a".repeat(64),
    outcome: "partly_reversed",
    rulesVersion: 2,
    redressVersion: 1,
    category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC",
    actions: [{ kind: "restore", mediaId: null }],

  };
  const stepUp = { id: "aWQ", rawId: "aWQ", type: "public-key", response: { clientDataJSON: "e30", authenticatorData: "AAAA", signature: "AAAA" }, clientExtensionResults: {} };

  test("is the action's params with the key's assertion beside them, and keeps the params' own rules", () => {
    expect(AppealsReviewedParams.parse(params)).toEqual(params);
    expect(AppealReviewRequest.safeParse({ ...params, stepUp }).success).toBe(true);
    expect(AppealReviewRequest.safeParse(params).success).toBe(false);
    // A review lifts and never restricts, with or without the assertion beside it.
    expect(AppealReviewRequest.safeParse({ ...params, actions: [{ kind: "remove", mediaId: null }], stepUp }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(AppealReviewRequest.safeParse({ ...params, outcome: "restricted", stepUp }).success).toBe(false);
    expect(AppealReviewRequest.safeParse({ ...params, reasonDigest: null, stepUp }).success).toBe(false);

});
```

```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import {
  ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE,
  ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE,
  ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN,
  CaseView,
  DecisionStatement,
  ITEM_OUTCOMES,
  OUTCOME_PHRASES,
  QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE,
  SEAL_DRAFTS,
  SUSPECT_NO_SEAL,
  SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES,
  StaffOverview,
  UNSEEN_NO_ACTION,
  outcomeWords,
  sealFactsDraft,
  type ItemOutcome,
  type OutcomeWordsInput,
} from "../src/index";

/**
 * The words a report's sender reads for an outcome, and the console's fixed drafts for a seal (3c design, section 10).
 * Each table is the one place its words are written: the mails, the status page, the app's list and the console take
 * them from here, so this file pins every word once.
 */
const RULE = { id: "R1", title: "No sexual or pornographic content" };

/** One item's facts, plain unless a test says otherwise: a post that quotes nothing, answered by a decision that saw its images. */
const words = (outcome: ItemOutcome, facts: Partial<OutcomeWordsInput> = {}): string =>
  outcomeWords({ outcome, rule: outcome === "restricted_rule" ? RULE : null, suspect: false, sealed: false, unseen: false, noEffect: false, scope: null, ...facts });

describe("the outcome phrases", () => {
  test("there is exactly one phrase for each outcome an item can be shown, word for word", () => {
    expect(Object.keys(OUTCOME_PHRASES).sort()).toEqual([...ITEM_OUTCOMES].sort());
    expect(OUTCOME_PHRASES).toEqual({
      restricted_rule: "access restricted: it breaks korbat rule {rule} ({title})",
      restricted_legal: "access restricted: korbat found it illegal",
      no_violation: "no action: korbat found no breach of its rules and nothing illegal",
      not_evident:
        "no action: korbat found no breach of its rules, and whether it is illegal cannot be seen without a detailed legal examination; a court or an authority can order its removal",
      not_available: "no action: the link names nothing korbat can show (checked automatically)",
      partly_reversed: "korbat reversed part of its decision to restrict it",
      reversed: "korbat reversed its decision to restrict it",
    });
  });

  test("the sentences that follow an outcome, and the phrases of the path for child sexual abuse material, word for word", () => {
    expect(ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN).toBe("It was already not shown on korbat, so nothing changed now; korbat's restriction stays in force should that change.");
    expect(ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE).toBe("This answer concerns the account's display name and bio. korbat decides about its posts and images in cases of their own and does not report those here.");
    expect(QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE).toBe(
      "This answer concerns this post's own text and images. korbat decides about the post it quotes, shown inside its card, in a case of its own and does not report that here.",
    );
    expect(ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE).toBe(
      "This answer concerns the account's display name and bio and, taken together, the images on its posts. korbat decides about single posts of the account, and about what its posts say, in cases of their own and does not report those here.",
    );
    expect(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES).toEqual({
      sealed: "access restricted: korbat sealed its images without opening them. They are shown to nobody, their author included, and are kept for the authorities.",
      no_action:
        "no action: korbat's staff do not open images reported this way. An admin found in the report, and in what korbat can read and still holds of it, no sufficient ground to seal images or to restrict anything else.",
    });
    expect(SUSPECT_NO_SEAL).toBe("No image was sealed; korbat's staff do not open images reported this way.");
    expect(UNSEEN_NO_ACTION).toBe(
      "no action for now: when korbat decided, its staff could not open this post's images, because a report of another kind about them was waiting or they were sealed. If your report is about an image, ask for a re-examination.",
    );
  });
});

describe("outcomeWords: one item's outcome as its sender reads it", () => {
  test("an ordinary item reads its outcome's phrase, a rule's with its id and title, and ends in one full stop", () => {
    expect(words("restricted_rule")).toBe("access restricted: it breaks korbat rule R1 (No sexual or pornographic content).");
    expect(words("restricted_legal")).toBe("access restricted: korbat found it illegal.");
    expect(words("no_violation")).toBe("no action: korbat found no breach of its rules and nothing illegal.");
    expect(words("not_evident")).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.not_evident}.`);
    expect(words("not_available")).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.not_available}.`);
    expect(words("partly_reversed")).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.partly_reversed}.`);
    expect(words("reversed")).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.reversed}.`);
    // A phrase that fills nothing in never keeps a placeholder, and no outcome ends in two full stops.
    for (const outcome of ITEM_OUTCOMES) {
      for (const facts of [{}, { suspect: true }, { sealed: true }, { unseen: true }, { noEffect: true }, { scope: "account" as const }, { scope: "quote" as const }, { scope: "account_suspect" as const }]) {
        const text = words(outcome, facts);
        expect(text, `${outcome} ${JSON.stringify(facts)}`).not.toMatch(/[{}]|[.][.]|[.] [.]/);
        expect(text.endsWith("."), `${outcome} ${JSON.stringify(facts)}`).toBe(true);
      }
    }
  });

  test("a restriction under a rule that is not named is refused: the phrase would keep its placeholder", () => {
    expect(() => outcomeWords({ outcome: "restricted_rule", rule: null, suspect: false, sealed: false, unseen: false, noEffect: false, scope: null })).toThrow(/rule/);
  });

  test("ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN follows a restricting outcome whose measures all changed nothing, a seal's included, and no other outcome", () => {
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { noEffect: true })).toBe(`access restricted: it breaks korbat rule R1 (No sexual or pornographic content). ${ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN}`);
    expect(words("restricted_legal", { noEffect: true })).toBe(`access restricted: korbat found it illegal. ${ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN}`);
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { noEffect: true, sealed: true })).toBe(`${SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed} ${ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN}`);
    for (const outcome of ["no_violation", "not_evident", "not_available", "partly_reversed", "reversed"] as const) expect(words(outcome, { noEffect: true }), outcome).not.toContain(ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN);
  });

  test("ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE follows the outcome of exactly the items about an account that are not suspect and whose decision sealed nothing", () => {
    for (const outcome of ITEM_OUTCOMES) {
      const text = words(outcome, { scope: "account" });
      expect(text.endsWith(` ${ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE}`), outcome).toBe(outcome !== "not_available");
      expect(text, outcome).not.toContain(ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE);
      for (const scope of [null, "quote", "account_suspect"] as const) expect(words(outcome, { scope }), `${outcome} ${String(scope)}`).not.toContain(ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE);
    }
    // After the already-not-shown sentence when both apply.
    expect(words("restricted_legal", { noEffect: true, scope: "account" })).toBe(`access restricted: korbat found it illegal. ${ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN} ${ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE}`);
  });

  test("QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE follows the outcome of exactly the items about a post that quotes another, after ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN when both apply", () => {
    for (const outcome of ITEM_OUTCOMES) {
      expect(words(outcome, { scope: "quote" }).endsWith(` ${QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE}`), outcome).toBe(outcome !== "not_available");
      for (const scope of [null, "account", "account_suspect"] as const) expect(words(outcome, { scope }), `${outcome} ${String(scope)}`).not.toContain(QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE);
    }
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { noEffect: true, scope: "quote" })).toBe(`access restricted: it breaks korbat rule R1 (No sexual or pornographic content). ${ALREADY_NOT_SHOWN} ${QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE}`);
  });

  test("ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE follows the outcome of exactly the items about an account that are suspect or that a sealing decision answered, a rule report merged into a sealed account case among them", () => {
    for (const outcome of ITEM_OUTCOMES) {
      expect(words(outcome, { scope: "account_suspect", suspect: true }).endsWith(` ${ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE}`), outcome).toBe(outcome !== "not_available");
      for (const scope of [null, "account", "quote"] as const) expect(words(outcome, { scope }), `${outcome} ${String(scope)}`).not.toContain(ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE);
    }
    // A rule report about an account that an answer with a seal answered: the sealed phrase, then the scope.
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { sealed: true, scope: "account_suspect" })).toBe(`${SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed} ${ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE}`);
  });

  test("a suspect item is worded from SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES, never from the four words for a finding alone", () => {
    expect(words("no_violation", { suspect: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.no_action);
    expect(words("not_evident", { suspect: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.no_action);
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { suspect: true, sealed: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed);
    expect(words("restricted_legal", { suspect: true, sealed: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed);
    // Answered by a measure on the post's text without a seal: the phrase of that finding, then that no image was sealed.
    expect(words("restricted_rule", { suspect: true })).toBe(`access restricted: it breaks korbat rule R1 (No sexual or pornographic content). ${SUSPECT_NO_SEAL}`);
    expect(words("restricted_legal", { suspect: true })).toBe(`access restricted: korbat found it illegal. ${SUSPECT_NO_SEAL}`);
    for (const outcome of ["no_violation", "not_evident", "restricted_rule", "restricted_legal"] as const) {
      for (const sealed of [false, true]) {
        const text = words(outcome, { suspect: true, sealed });
        expect(text === `${OUTCOME_PHRASES[outcome]}.` || text === "access restricted: it breaks korbat rule R1 (No sexual or pornographic content).", `${outcome} ${sealed}`).toBe(false);
      }
    }
    // The other three outcomes are worded as for any item.
    expect(words("not_available", { suspect: true })).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.not_available}.`);
    expect(words("partly_reversed", { suspect: true, sealed: true })).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.partly_reversed}.`);
    expect(words("reversed", { suspect: true, sealed: true })).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.reversed}.`);
  });

  test("the sealed phrase stands for every item a sealing decision answered, suspect or not, in place of both restricting phrases", () => {
    for (const suspect of [false, true]) {
      expect(words("restricted_rule", { sealed: true, suspect })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed);
      expect(words("restricted_legal", { sealed: true, suspect })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.sealed);
    }

  test("an item on another ground about a post, answered without action while nobody could open its images, reads UNSEEN_NO_ACTION, and no other item does", () => {

    expect(words("not_evident", { unseen: true })).toBe(UNSEEN_NO_ACTION);
    // A restriction, a reversal and a link that named nothing keep their own words, and a suspect item its own phrase.
    for (const outcome of ["restricted_rule", "restricted_legal", "not_available", "partly_reversed", "reversed"] as const) expect(words(outcome, { unseen: true }), outcome).not.toContain(UNSEEN_NO_ACTION);
    expect(words("no_violation", { unseen: true, suspect: true })).toBe(SUSPECT_OUTCOME_PHRASES.no_action);
    // An item about an account is never worded this way, whatever its decision's mark: it keeps the ordinary phrase with its scope.
    expect(words("no_violation", { unseen: true, scope: "account" })).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.no_violation}. ${ACCOUNT_ITEM_SCOPE}`);
    expect(words("not_evident", { unseen: true, scope: "account_suspect" })).toBe(`${OUTCOME_PHRASES.not_evident}. ${ACCOUNT_SUSPECT_SCOPE}`);
    // On a post that quotes another the scope follows it as it follows any outcome.
    expect(words("no_violation", { unseen: true, scope: "quote" })).toBe(`${UNSEEN_NO_ACTION} ${QUOTE_ITEM_SCOPE}`);
  });
});

describe("the console's fixed drafts for a seal", () => {
  test("SEAL_DRAFTS holds its eight texts, word for word", () => {
    expect(SEAL_DRAFTS).toEqual({
      facts: {
        notice_post: "korbat received a notice that reports images of this post as child sexual abuse material.",
        notice_account: "korbat received a notice that reports this account for child sexual abuse material. It does not say which images, so korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
        notice_added: "korbat received a notice about content on korbat that shows this post's images and reports them as child sexual abuse material.",
        finding_post: "A moderator reported images of this post as possible child sexual abuse material.",
        finding_account: "A moderator reported images on this account's posts as possible child sexual abuse material. korbat sealed every image on the account's posts.",
        finding_added: "A moderator reported content on korbat that shows this post's images as possible child sexual abuse material.",
      },
      reason: {
        deciding: "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. It hides them from everyone, you included, until an admin has answered the report.",
        final:
          "korbat's staff do not open images reported this way, so korbat has not assessed them. An admin found the report credible enough to keep the images sealed and to report them to the police, who can assess them.",
      },
    });
    expect(Object.keys(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts).length + Object.keys(SEAL_DRAFTS.reason).length).toBe(8);
  });

  test("none says that korbat found the images to be such material, and each reason says that staff do not open them", () => {
    for (const text of [...Object.values(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts), ...Object.values(SEAL_DRAFTS.reason)]) {
      expect(text).not.toMatch(/korbat found|is child sexual abuse material|are child sexual abuse material/);
    }
    for (const text of Object.values(SEAL_DRAFTS.reason)) expect(text).toContain("korbat's staff do not open images reported this way");
    // The two drafts for an added item never say that this post was reported, and name no other post.
    for (const text of [SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_added, SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.finding_added]) expect(text).not.toMatch(/of this post as|this post was|quot/);
  });

  test("the facts draft follows the suspect items the decision considers: a notice when any came from a user, the added form when every one was added by korbat, else by the case's target", () => {
    const item = (source: "user" | "finding", added = false) => ({ source, added });
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("user")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("account", [item("user")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_account);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("finding")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.finding_post);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("account", [item("finding")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.finding_account);
    // A notice among findings makes it a notice's draft.
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("finding"), item("user")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post);
    // Every item added for a quoted post (or a re-examination of one): the added form; one named item among them: the post's.
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("user", true), item("user", true)])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_added);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("finding", true)])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.finding_added);
    expect(sealFactsDraft("post", [item("user", true), item("finding")])).toBe(SEAL_DRAFTS.facts.notice_post);
    expect(() => sealFactsDraft("post", [])).toThrow(/suspect item/);
  });
});
```

```ts
/**
 * The console's requests and answers on cases (3c design, section 10): what a moderator's own finding may say, what a
 * saved text must be, and the shapes the queue, the case and the home screen are parsed with.
 */

const CASE = "3f1c2b1e-8d4a-4c1e-9b2a-6f0e5d4c3b2a";
const POST = "7e2d9a10-6c3b-4f5e-8a21-0d4c7b9e1f36";
```
