### Create `apps/api/src/moderation/retention.ts`

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { RETENTION } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID } from "../auth";
import { createJob, type JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import { DISPOSAL_BATCH } from "../media";
import { appendAuditRow } from "../staff";
import type { ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { deleteAccessLog, dueCases, dueIntakes, dueRedactions, dueStatements, eraseCaseEvidence, eraseIntake, eraseStatementTexts, redactR4, sweepStaffTexts } from "./repo";

/**
 * The retention job (3c design, sections 6.4, 6.6 and 7.9): every ten minutes it deletes the drafts nobody confirmed,
 * erases the evidence of the cases and the records of the intakes that are due, makes R4 redactions final, erases the
 * statements of accounts deleted for 12 months, deletes the old access rows, and deletes the image rows that a case or a
 * freeze kept and nothing retains any more.
 *
 * The job only names what it believes is due. Each erase function of migration 0018 checks its own rule again, against
 * values the API role cannot set, and the two gates of the freeze decide for every snapshot and every image row: so a
 * wrong candidate, or an API that asks early, erases nothing.
 *
 * Every step, and within a step every row, runs in a transaction of its own, which ends with one audit row when it
 * changed something and writes nothing when it did not. A row that raises is rolled back alone, logged with the step and
 * the row's id, and tried again at the next round: a case that keeps failing never stops another case's erasure. No log
 * line carries an address, a handle or an account id.
 */

const MINUTE_MS = 60_000;

/** The job's name: its lock is `job:moderation-retention`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const RETENTION_JOB = "moderation-retention";
/** The time between the end of one round and the start of the next. */
export const RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * MINUTE_MS;
/** The audit action of every step that changed something. It is written by the server itself, never under a step-up. */
export const RETENTION_ACTION = "moderation_retention";
/** What the API logs at every start while the job is switched off, which the README's restore steps do for a restore window. */
export const RETENTION_OFF_WARNING = "moderation-retention: off (MODERATION_RETENTION)";

/** The steps, by the name their audit rows and log lines carry. */
export type RetentionStep = "drafts" | "case_evidence" | "intake_record" | "redaction" | "statements" | "access_log" | "images";

/** What one round did, for its log line and for the tests: counts only. */
export interface RetentionReport {
  /** The drafts deleted. */
  drafts: number;
  /** The cases whose evidence was erased, the intakes whose record was, the R4 decisions redacted and the decisions whose statements were erased. */
  cases: number;
  intakes: number;
  redactions: number;
  statements: number;
  /** The access rows deleted, with the reveal reasons erased before them. */
  accessLog: number;
  /** The size of each batch of image rows the disposal deleted, in order; the last one is smaller than a full batch. */
  batches: number[];
  /** The steps and rows that raised and were left for the next round. */
  failed: number;
}

/** The ids a step's audit row names; each is null where the step has none. */
interface StepIds {
  caseId?: string;
  intakeId?: string;
  decisionId?: string;
}

/**
 * One step, or one row of a step, in a transaction of its own: the change, then its audit row as the transaction's last
 * statement, since the insert holds the chain's head until the commit. A change of nothing writes nothing. A lock is
 * waited on for at most ten seconds, so a transaction left open elsewhere costs this row a round, never the job.
 */
async function inStep(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, step: RetentionStep, ids: StepIds, change: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<number>): Promise<number> {
  return deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
    const count = await change(tx);
    if (count > 0) {
      await appendAuditRow(tx, {
        actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID,
        action: RETENTION_ACTION,
        targetType: null,
        targetId: null,
        requestId: null,
        // Ids and counts only, never a text.
        metadata: { step, caseId: ids.caseId ?? null, intakeId: ids.intakeId ?? null, decisionId: ids.decisionId ?? null, count },
      });
    }
    return count;
  });
}

/**
 * The disposal: the one deleter of image rows that a case or a freeze kept, in batches. Each batch is a transaction of
 * its own with its audit row, and its files are requested right after its commit and before the next batch. They are
 * never requested before the commit: a disposable row is not disposable for good (a report may freeze a deleted post's
 * images at any moment), so a batch rolled back after its request would lose the files of rows a freeze then keeps. A
 * request lost to a crash names at most one batch, which the reconcile pass makes good. When a request fails the step
 * stops for this round, so that no second batch's files join the first's as orphans.
 */
async function dispose(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log">, report: RetentionReport): Promise<void> {
  for (;;) {
    let ids: string[] = [];
    await inStep(deps, "images", {}, async (tx) => {
      ids = await deps.media.dropDisposable(tx);
      return ids.length;
    });
    report.batches.push(ids.length);
    if (ids.length > 0) {
      try {
        await deps.media.requestDeletion(ids);
      } catch (err) {
        report.failed++;
        deps.log.error({ err, job: RETENTION_JOB, step: "images", count: ids.length }, "moderation-retention: the files of a deleted batch could not be requested; the reconcile pass removes them, and the disposal goes on at the next round");
        return;
      }
    }
    if (ids.length < DISPOSAL_BATCH) return;
  }
}

/** One round. A plain function, so the tests call it directly. */
export async function retentionRound(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log">): Promise<RetentionReport> {
  const report: RetentionReport = { drafts: 0, cases: 0, intakes: 0, redactions: 0, statements: 0, accessLog: 0, batches: [], failed: 0 };
  /** A step in a try of its own: what it raises is logged with the step, and the round goes on. */
  const step = async (name: RetentionStep, run: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      await run();
    } catch (err) {
      report.failed++;
      deps.log.error({ err, job: RETENTION_JOB, step: name }, "moderation-retention: a step failed; the round goes on");
    }
  };
  /** Each row of a step in a try of its own, under the row's id. */
  const each = async (name: RetentionStep, key: keyof StepIds, ids: readonly string[], change: (tx: DbTx, id: string) => Promise<number>): Promise<number> => {
    let done = 0;
    for (const id of ids) {
      try {
        if ((await inStep(deps, name, { [key]: id }, (tx) => change(tx, id))) > 0) done++;
      } catch (err) {
        report.failed++;
        deps.log.error({ err, job: RETENTION_JOB, step: name, [key]: id }, "moderation-retention: a row failed and was left as it was; the round goes on");
      }
    }
    return done;
  };

  await step("drafts", async () => {
    report.drafts = await inStep(deps, "drafts", {}, (tx) => sweepStaffTexts(tx, RETENTION.draftHours));
  });
  await step("case_evidence", async () => {
    report.cases = await each("case_evidence", "caseId", await dueCases(deps.apiDb), eraseCaseEvidence);
  });
  await step("intake_record", async () => {
    report.intakes = await each("intake_record", "intakeId", await dueIntakes(deps.apiDb, RETENTION.intakeDays), eraseIntake);
  });
  // The redaction answers false, and nothing is written, while its post is frozen: the next round asks again.
  await step("redaction", async () => {
    report.redactions = await each("redaction", "decisionId", await dueRedactions(deps.apiDb), async (tx, id) => ((await redactR4(tx, id)) ? 1 : 0));
  });
  await step("statements", async () => {
    report.statements = await each("statements", "decisionId", await dueStatements(deps.apiDb, RETENTION.statementMonths), eraseStatementTexts);
  });
  await step("access_log", async () => {
    report.accessLog = await inStep(deps, "access_log", {}, (tx) => deleteAccessLog(tx, RETENTION.accessLogMonths));
  });
  await step("images", () => dispose(deps, report));

  // One line for a round that did something or failed somewhere: counts only.
  const images = report.batches.reduce((sum, size) => sum + size, 0);
  if (report.drafts + report.cases + report.intakes + report.redactions + report.statements + report.accessLog + images + report.failed > 0) {
    deps.log.info({ job: RETENTION_JOB, ...report, images }, "moderation-retention: round");
  }
  return report;
}

/** The job: a round every ten minutes, counted from the end of the one before, on one API instance at a time. */
export function createRetentionJob(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log">, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: RETENTION_JOB, intervalMs: RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => retentionRound(deps) });
}
```

### Create `packages/db/migrations/0018_retention.sql`

```sql
-- Retention (3c design, section 6.4). Written by hand: this migration changes no table. Each kind of data has a due rule
-- of its own, read only from the anchors of the data it erases, and an erase function of its own, which checks that rule
-- itself against values the API role cannot set: so the retention job names what it believes is due, and the database
-- decides. No due rule knows the freeze of the path for suspected child sexual abuse material: a frozen post's snapshots
-- are kept by erase_snapshots (gate E), the one function that erases a snapshot, and its image rows by the keep trigger
-- of migration 0015 (gate K), which every erase function and every delete meets. As in 0016 and 0017, every function is
-- owned by the migrator, pins its search path, names every object schema-qualified and has EXECUTE taken from PUBLIC;
-- errors carry their code as the message under SQLSTATE P0001 unless a SQLSTATE is named; and a read that follows a lock is
-- a statement of its own, which under READ COMMITTED sees every row committed while the lock waited. The periods (24
-- hours, 30 days, 12 months) are the contracts' RETENTION, which a database test holds these functions to.
--
-- When a decision is final for its author: for a final decision that restricts, the answer to the author's appeal (null
-- while one is pending) or, when none was filed, the end of the appeal's window; for every other decision the moment it
-- was taken, since what korbat does while it decides, a decision without action, a review and a correction cannot be
-- appealed. Null for an id that names no decision.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."decision_final_at"(decision_id uuid) RETURNS timestamptz
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT CASE
           WHEN d.kind = 'final' AND d.outcome = 'restricted'
             THEN CASE WHEN a.id IS NULL THEN public.appeal_deadline(d.informed_at) ELSE a.answered_at END
           ELSE d.decided_at
         END
    FROM public.decisions d
    LEFT JOIN public.appeals a ON a.decision_id = d.id
   WHERE d.id = decision_final_at.decision_id
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."decision_final_at"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."decision_final_at"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- When a case's evidence (its snapshots, notes, draft texts, appeal statements and holds) is due. Null, which is "not
-- due", while the case is open, and while a final restriction of the case with a measure in force is not yet final for its
-- author. Otherwise the latest of: the case's close; when those restrictions became final; 24 hours after the case's
-- newest unerased snapshot and its newest unconfirmed, unerased text, so that a snapshot or a draft taken on a case
-- already due, for a correction or a review, is not erased under the person using it; and 30 days after each field reset
-- of the case stopped being in force (its reversal, or the case's close for a reset taken while deciding), so that the
-- person can read the old value on the screen of the decision that reset it for at least that long. It reads nothing
-- about items, mails, releases, notifiers or the freeze.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."case_evidence_due_at"(case_id uuid) RETURNS timestamptz
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT CASE
           WHEN c.closed_at IS NULL THEN NULL
           WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.decisions d
                         WHERE d.case_id = c.id AND d.kind = 'final' AND d.outcome = 'restricted'
                           AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force m WHERE m.decision_id = d.id)
                           AND coalesce(public.decision_final_at(d.id) > now(), true)) THEN NULL
           ELSE greatest(
             c.closed_at,
             (SELECT max(public.decision_final_at(d.id)) FROM public.decisions d
               WHERE d.case_id = c.id AND d.kind = 'final' AND d.outcome = 'restricted'
                 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force m WHERE m.decision_id = d.id)),
             (SELECT max(s.taken_at) + interval '24 hours' FROM public.evidence_snapshots s WHERE s.case_id = c.id AND s.erased_at IS NULL),
             (SELECT max(t.created_at) + interval '24 hours' FROM public.staff_texts t
               WHERE t.case_id = c.id AND t.confirmed_at IS NULL AND t.erased_at IS NULL),
             (SELECT max(coalesce(r.created_at, c.closed_at)) + interval '30 days'
                FROM public.decision_actions a
                JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = a.decision_id
                LEFT JOIN public.decision_actions r ON r.reverses_action_id = a.id
               WHERE d.case_id = c.id AND a.kind IN ('reset_display_name', 'reset_bio')
                 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.measures_in_force m WHERE m.id = a.id)))
         END
    FROM public.cases c
   WHERE c.id = case_evidence_due_at.case_id
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."case_evidence_due_at"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."case_evidence_due_at"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- When an intake's record (its explanation, its cited law, who sent it and its re-examinations' statements) is due. Null
-- while korbat still owes any of its items something: an answer (a re-examination included), the release of an outcome or
-- of a changed outcome, a mail, or the chance to ask for a re-examination, which is open by the attach trigger's own rule
-- (a moderator's answer without action, released, inside the six months, not re-examined, and either no re-examination
-- itself or one about a post that is not suspect, answered while nobody could open the post's images); and while a
-- restriction that answered one of its items is not yet final for its author, so that a reversal on the author's appeal
-- still reaches a signed-in reporter. Otherwise 30 days after the last release, while the reporter's list shows it.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."intake_due_at"(intake_id uuid) RETURNS timestamptz
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT CASE
           WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.intake_items i
                         LEFT JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = i.answered_by
                        WHERE i.intake_id = n.id
                          AND (i.outcome IS NULL
                            OR i.revision_pending_at IS NOT NULL
                            OR i.outcome_sent_at IS NULL
                            OR i.outcome_mail = 'pending'
                            OR (i.outcome IN ('no_violation', 'not_evident') AND i.answered_by IS NOT NULL
                                AND public.appeal_deadline(i.outcome_sent_at) > now()
                                AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.intake_items x WHERE x.reexamines_item_id = i.id)
                                AND (i.reexamines_item_id IS NULL OR (i.target_type = 'post' AND NOT i.suspect AND d.unseen)))
                            OR (d.outcome = 'restricted' AND coalesce(public.decision_final_at(d.id) > now(), true)))) THEN NULL
           ELSE (SELECT max(greatest(i.outcome_sent_at, i.revised_sent_at)) + interval '30 days'
                   FROM public.intake_items i WHERE i.intake_id = n.id)
         END
    FROM public.intakes n
   WHERE n.id = intake_due_at.intake_id
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."intake_due_at"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."intake_due_at"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- Erases a case's evidence once it is due, and answers how many rows it changed. First the case's row FOR UPDATE: that
-- waits for a decision on the case, for an appeal being filed (which holds the row FOR KEY SHARE) and for the insert of
-- a snapshot or a text (their foreign keys hold it the same way); then the due time is read in a statement of its own,
-- which sees what they committed (without the lock, a decision that had read its snapshot unerased committed naming a
-- snapshot the erasure had just erased). A null due time is not due. It then erases the case's unerased snapshots
-- through the one function that erases a snapshot, which keeps those of a frozen post; the case's notes and unconfirmed
-- texts (a text a decision confirmed is that decision's statement, kept until its own rule erases it); and the statements
-- of the appeals of the case's decisions, each with its digest kept. Last it releases the case's holds, which frees no
-- image of a frozen post: the keep trigger holds those whether a hold stands or not. It touches no intake.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."erase_case_evidence"(case_id uuid) RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  due timestamptz;
  changed integer;
  n integer;
BEGIN
  PERFORM 1 FROM public.cases c WHERE c.id = erase_case_evidence.case_id FOR UPDATE;
  SELECT public.case_evidence_due_at(erase_case_evidence.case_id) INTO due;
  IF due IS NULL OR due > now() THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'not_due';
  END IF;

  SELECT public.erase_snapshots(ARRAY(SELECT s.id FROM public.evidence_snapshots s
                                       WHERE s.case_id = erase_case_evidence.case_id AND s.erased_at IS NULL)) INTO changed;

  UPDATE public.staff_texts t SET text = NULL, salt = NULL, erased_at = now()
   WHERE t.case_id = erase_case_evidence.case_id AND t.confirmed_at IS NULL AND t.erased_at IS NULL;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  changed := changed + n;

  UPDATE public.appeals a SET statement = NULL, statement_salt = NULL, erased_at = now()
   WHERE a.statement IS NOT NULL
     AND a.decision_id IN (SELECT d.id FROM public.decisions d WHERE d.case_id = erase_case_evidence.case_id);
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  changed := changed + n;

  SELECT public.release_case_holds(erase_case_evidence.case_id, NULL) INTO n;
  RETURN changed + n;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."erase_case_evidence"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."erase_case_evidence"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- Gate E: the one function that erases a snapshot's content, and the only writer of evidence_snapshots.erased_at. In one
-- statement it erases each named snapshot that is not erased yet (the content columns and the salt null, the digest, the
-- handles, the ids and the times kept), except a snapshot of a post that is frozen: so no path erases a snapshot of a
-- frozen post, in whatever case the snapshot is, and no due rule needs a term for it. It answers how many it erased. It
-- judges the freeze on its statement's snapshot: a suspect item that commits during that statement is not seen, and the
-- outcome equals "erased first, reported second". Outside READ COMMITTED that read would see the transaction's old
-- snapshot, so it refuses to run there (read_committed_only, as the keep trigger does). Nobody may call it: the two
-- erasures of this migration do, as its owner.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."erase_snapshots"(snapshots uuid[]) RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  n integer;
BEGIN
  IF current_setting('transaction_isolation') <> 'read committed' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'read_committed_only' USING ERRCODE = '25000';
  END IF;
  UPDATE public.evidence_snapshots s
     SET erased_at = now(), body = NULL, media = NULL, display_name = NULL, bio = NULL, salt = NULL
   WHERE s.id = ANY(erase_snapshots.snapshots) AND s.erased_at IS NULL
     AND NOT (s.target_type = 'post' AND public.post_frozen(s.target_id));
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RETURN n;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."erase_snapshots"(uuid[]) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
-- Erases an intake's record once it is due, and answers how many rows it changed. First the intake's row FOR UPDATE,
-- which a re-examination waits for (the attach trigger holds the row FOR KEY SHARE and then refuses an erased intake);
-- then the due time, in a statement of its own. It nulls the explanation and the cited law and marks the intake erased
-- (its good-faith statement stays), forgets who sent it, on the intake and on its items, so that who reported whom goes
-- with the record, and erases its re-examinations' statements, each with its digest kept.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."erase_intake"(intake_id uuid) RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  due timestamptz;
  changed integer;
  n integer;
BEGIN
  PERFORM 1 FROM public.intakes k WHERE k.id = erase_intake.intake_id FOR UPDATE;
  SELECT public.intake_due_at(erase_intake.intake_id) INTO due;
  IF due IS NULL OR due > now() THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'not_due';
  END IF;

  UPDATE public.intakes k SET explanation = NULL, cited_law = NULL, reporter_id = NULL, erased_at = now()
   WHERE k.id = erase_intake.intake_id AND k.erased_at IS NULL;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS changed = ROW_COUNT;

  UPDATE public.intake_items i SET reporter_account_id = NULL
   WHERE i.intake_id = erase_intake.intake_id AND i.reporter_account_id IS NOT NULL;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  changed := changed + n;

  UPDATE public.intake_items i SET statement = NULL, statement_salt = NULL, erased_at = now()
   WHERE i.intake_id = erase_intake.intake_id AND i.statement IS NOT NULL;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RETURN changed + n;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."erase_intake"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."erase_intake"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- Erases a decision's statement texts (its facts, its reason and its legal reference; for a review or a correction the
-- reason it gave), each with its digest kept, once the decision's subject account has been deleted for 12 months, and
-- answers how many it erased. The retention job finds its candidates by the profile's deletion mark, which the API role
-- can write; this function decides by the auth row's mark, which the API's other role can set only to now() and never
-- clear (users_deleted_mark, below), so code running as the API cannot erase a live account's statements. The take-down
-- marks the auth row before the purge marks the profile, so the function never refuses a decision the job names in good
-- faith. The decision's row is locked first, so two erasures of one decision run one after the other.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."erase_statement_texts"(decision_id uuid) RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  d public.decisions;
  subject uuid;
  deleted timestamptz;
  n integer;
BEGIN
  SELECT x.* INTO d FROM public.decisions x WHERE x.id = erase_statement_texts.decision_id FOR NO KEY UPDATE;
  IF NOT FOUND THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'not_due';
  END IF;

    INTO subject

  IF deleted IS NULL OR deleted > now() - interval '12 months' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'not_due';
  END IF;
  UPDATE public.staff_texts t SET text = NULL, salt = NULL, erased_at = now()
   WHERE t.digest IN (d.facts_digest, d.reason_digest, d.legal_reference_digest) AND t.erased_at IS NULL;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RETURN n;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- The R4 redaction: content restricted under rule R4 (personal information) is erased once the restriction is final for
-- its author, a one-way erasure keyed on the decision's measures in force. True when it changed something. In this order:
--   1. It refuses (invalid_decision) any decision that is not final, does not cite R4, or holds no removal of a post or
--      an image and no field reset.
--   2. Its locks, before it writes anything, in the order of every other transaction that touches moderation: for an
--      account case the profile's row FOR NO KEY UPDATE; the decision's case FOR UPDATE, so it waits for a decision on the
--      case or an appeal being filed and sees their commits; for a post case the post's row FOR UPDATE and then, in a
--      statement of its own, every image row of the post in id order FOR NO KEY UPDATE. Writing an image's erasure mark
--      before locking the post's images in order deadlocked with an intake locking the same images.
--   3. Then, each in a statement of its own: it refuses to run outside READ COMMITTED (read_committed_only), where its
--      reads would see the transaction's old snapshot; it refuses (not_due) a decision that is not yet final for its
--      author; and it changes nothing and answers false unless the decision is not redacted yet and one of its R4 measures
--      is in force, whatever the post's lifecycle (the author's deletion and the purge leave korbat's copies, which must
--      still go). For a post case it also changes nothing and answers false while the post is frozen: the post's body,
--      its images and its snapshots in every case then wait for the end of the freeze, and the caller tries again later.
--   4. For a post removal in force it blanks the post's body and marks the post erased, which removes it for good; for
--      an image removal in force it marks that image erased. The post's mark is set only for a post-level removal. A mark
--      that is already set keeps its time: the content went then.
--   5. It erases, through the one function that erases a snapshot, every unerased snapshot of the decision's target (the
--      post, or the account), in this case and in any other, so no copy of the content outlives the restriction's
--      finality.
--   6. It marks the decision redacted only when no unerased snapshot of that target is left in any case. When the
--      freeze began between step 3 and step 5 (a suspect item about the author's account locks no row this function
--      holds), a snapshot was kept, the decision stays a candidate, and the call after the freeze ends finishes it.
--   7. It releases the case's holds on the images it erased (every image of the post for a post removal, that image for
--      an image removal); the case's other holds stay its evidence. For a post case it then derives the post's level and
--      its images' states again: an erased post is removed, and so is an erased image.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."redact_r4_body"(decision_id uuid) RETURNS boolean
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  d public.decisions;
  c public.cases;
  final_at timestamptz;
  redacted timestamptz;
  in_force boolean;
  removes boolean;
  frozen boolean;
  removed_images uuid[];
  released uuid[];
BEGIN
  -- 1.
  SELECT x.* INTO d FROM public.decisions x WHERE x.id = redact_r4_body.decision_id;
  IF NOT FOUND OR d.kind <> 'final' OR d.rule_id IS DISTINCT FROM 'R4'
     OR NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.decision_actions a
                     WHERE a.decision_id = d.id AND a.kind IN ('remove', 'remove_media', 'reset_bio', 'reset_display_name')) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid_decision';
  END IF;
  -- A decision's case and a case's target never change, so this read before the locks names the right rows.
  SELECT k.* INTO c FROM public.cases k WHERE k.id = d.case_id;

  -- 2.
  IF c.target_type = 'account' THEN
    PERFORM 1 FROM public.profiles p WHERE p.id = c.target_id FOR NO KEY UPDATE;
  END IF;
  PERFORM 1 FROM public.cases k WHERE k.id = c.id FOR UPDATE;
  IF c.target_type = 'post' THEN
    PERFORM 1 FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = c.target_id FOR UPDATE;
    PERFORM 1 FROM public.post_media m WHERE m.post_id = c.target_id ORDER BY m.id FOR NO KEY UPDATE;
  END IF;

  -- 3.
  IF current_setting('transaction_isolation') <> 'read committed' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'read_committed_only' USING ERRCODE = '25000';
  END IF;
  SELECT public.decision_final_at(d.id) INTO final_at;
  IF final_at IS NULL OR final_at > now() THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'not_due';
  END IF;
  SELECT x.redacted_at INTO redacted FROM public.decisions x WHERE x.id = d.id;
  IF redacted IS NOT NULL THEN
    RETURN false;
  END IF;
  SELECT count(*) > 0, coalesce(bool_or(f.kind = 'remove'), false), coalesce(array_agg(f.media_id) FILTER (WHERE f.kind = 'remove_media'), '{}'::uuid[])
    INTO in_force, removes, removed_images
    FROM public.measures_in_force f
   WHERE f.decision_id = d.id AND f.kind IN ('remove', 'remove_media', 'reset_bio', 'reset_display_name');
  IF NOT in_force THEN
    RETURN false;
  END IF;
  IF c.target_type = 'post' THEN
    SELECT public.post_frozen(c.target_id) INTO frozen;
    IF frozen THEN
      RETURN false;
    END IF;
  END IF;

  -- 4.
  released := removed_images;
  IF removes THEN
    UPDATE public.posts p SET body = '', erased_at = coalesce(p.erased_at, now()) WHERE p.id = c.target_id;
    SELECT coalesce(array_agg(m.id), '{}'::uuid[]) INTO released FROM public.post_media m WHERE m.post_id = c.target_id;
  END IF;
  IF cardinality(removed_images) > 0 THEN
    UPDATE public.post_media m SET erased_at = coalesce(m.erased_at, now()) WHERE m.id = ANY(removed_images) AND m.post_id = c.target_id;
  END IF;

  -- 5.
  PERFORM public.erase_snapshots(ARRAY(SELECT s.id FROM public.evidence_snapshots s
                                        WHERE s.target_type = c.target_type AND s.target_id = c.target_id AND s.erased_at IS NULL));

  -- 6.
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.evidence_snapshots s
                  WHERE s.target_type = c.target_type AND s.target_id = c.target_id AND s.erased_at IS NULL) THEN
    UPDATE public.decisions x SET redacted_at = now() WHERE x.id = d.id;
  END IF;

  -- 7.
  PERFORM public.release_case_holds(c.id, released);
  IF c.target_type = 'post' THEN
    PERFORM public.moderation_apply(ARRAY[c.target_id], true);
  END IF;
  RETURN true;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."redact_r4_body"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint

-- Deletes the staff texts nobody confirmed (never a note or a recorded choice not to seal, which are never confirmed and
-- go with their case's evidence, and never a confirmed text) that were saved before the given time, and answers how many.
-- It refuses (not_due) a time less than 24 hours back, so no caller deletes a draft a moderator is still working on.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."sweep_staff_texts"(older_than timestamptz) RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  n integer;
BEGIN
  IF sweep_staff_texts.older_than IS NULL OR sweep_staff_texts.older_than > now() - interval '24 hours' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'not_due';
  END IF;
  DELETE FROM public.staff_texts t
   WHERE t.kind NOT IN ('note', 'seal_declined') AND t.confirmed_at IS NULL AND t.created_at < sweep_staff_texts.older_than;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RETURN n;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."sweep_staff_texts"(timestamptz) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."sweep_staff_texts"(timestamptz) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- Deletes the access rows older than the given time, and answers how many rows it changed. It first erases the reveal
-- reasons that the reveals among them name (text and salt null, the digest kept): a reason is kept as long as the access
-- row that names it. It refuses (not_due) a time less than 12 months back.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."delete_access_log"(older_than timestamptz) RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  changed integer;
  n integer;
BEGIN
  IF delete_access_log.older_than IS NULL OR delete_access_log.older_than > now() - interval '12 months' THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'not_due';
  END IF;
  UPDATE public.staff_texts t SET text = NULL, salt = NULL, erased_at = now()
   WHERE t.kind = 'reveal_reason' AND t.erased_at IS NULL
     AND t.id IN (SELECT l.text_id FROM public.case_access_log l
                   WHERE l.kind = 'identity_revealed' AND l.text_id IS NOT NULL AND l.at < delete_access_log.older_than);
  GET DIAGNOSTICS changed = ROW_COUNT;
  DELETE FROM public.case_access_log l WHERE l.at < delete_access_log.older_than;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RETURN changed + n;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."delete_access_log"(timestamptz) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."delete_access_log"(timestamptz) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- Forgets that a deleted account sent its reports: the reporter's id goes from its intakes and from their items, and the
-- intakes go on being processed. It acts only on an account whose auth row is marked deleted, read here, and changes
-- nothing for any other: the take-down sets that mark before any step of the purge, so the purge's call finds it. It
-- answers how many rows it changed, 0 when run again.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."forget_reporter"(account uuid) RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  changed integer;
  n integer;
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM auth.users u WHERE u.id = forget_reporter.account AND u.deleted_at IS NOT NULL) THEN
    RETURN 0;
  END IF;
  UPDATE public.intakes k SET reporter_id = NULL WHERE k.reporter_id = forget_reporter.account;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS changed = ROW_COUNT;
  UPDATE public.intake_items i SET reporter_account_id = NULL WHERE i.reporter_account_id = forget_reporter.account;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS n = ROW_COUNT;
  RETURN changed + n;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."forget_reporter"(uuid) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."forget_reporter"(uuid) TO korbat_api;--> statement-breakpoint
-- An account's deletion mark, held against the API's other role. The API holds korbat_auth too: without this trigger,
-- code running as the API could back-date a live account's mark, call erase_statement_texts or forget_reporter above, and
-- clear the mark again. For korbat_auth a mark that is set can be neither cleared nor changed (SQLSTATE 23514), and a
-- mark set from null becomes now(), whatever value was supplied: no code clears the mark, and now() replaces the
-- take-down's own time with its transaction's start. The function is plain, so current_user is the role that ran the
-- statement. The migrator, and tests that move the clock as it, are not bound.
CREATE FUNCTION "auth"."users_deleted_mark"() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = auth, pg_temp AS $$
BEGIN
  IF current_user = 'korbat_auth' THEN
    IF OLD.deleted_at IS NOT NULL THEN
      IF NEW.deleted_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.deleted_at THEN
        RAISE EXCEPTION 'an account''s deletion mark is never cleared or changed (users_deleted_mark)'
          USING ERRCODE = '23514', TABLE = 'users', CONSTRAINT = 'users_deleted_mark';
      END IF;
    ELSIF NEW.deleted_at IS NOT NULL THEN
      NEW.deleted_at := now();
    END IF;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "auth"."users_deleted_mark"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
CREATE TRIGGER "users_deleted_mark" BEFORE UPDATE OF "deleted_at" ON "auth"."users" FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION "auth"."users_deleted_mark"();--> statement-breakpoint
-- Releases a case's holds, one row at a time in the order of their images' ids, which is the order every other
-- transaction locks image rows in (each release takes its image's row through the trigger that keeps hold_until): every
-- unreleased hold of the case when no image is named, otherwise only those on the named images. It answers how many it
-- released. Nobody may call it: the two erasures of this migration do, as its owner.
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."release_case_holds"(case_id uuid, media uuid[]) RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  hold bigint;
  n integer := 0;
BEGIN
  FOR hold IN
    SELECT h.id FROM public.media_holds h
     WHERE h.case_id = release_case_holds.case_id AND h.released_at IS NULL
       AND (release_case_holds.media IS NULL OR h.media_id = ANY(release_case_holds.media))
     ORDER BY h.media_id, h.id
  LOOP
    UPDATE public.media_holds h SET released_at = now() WHERE h.id = hold AND h.released_at IS NULL;
    IF FOUND THEN
      n := n + 1;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
  RETURN n;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."release_case_holds"(uuid, uuid[]) FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
-- How many personal accounts each staff account has linked: one row for each staff account with at least one link, never
-- which accounts. `staff.js keys` prints the counts for the operator's comparison with their own records; the auth role
-- holds nothing on the table itself.
CREATE FUNCTION "auth"."staff_link_counts"() RETURNS TABLE (staff_user_id uuid, links integer)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = auth, pg_temp AS $$
  SELECT l.staff_user_id, count(*)::integer FROM auth.staff_personal_accounts l GROUP BY l.staff_user_id
$$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "auth"."staff_link_counts"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "auth"."staff_link_counts"() TO korbat_auth;
```

```json
        "decisions_api_all": {
          "name": "decisions_api_all",
          "as": "PERMISSIVE",
          "for": "ALL",
          "to": [
            "korbat_api"
          ],
          "using": "true",
          "withCheck": "true"
        }
      },
      "checkConstraints": {
        "decisions_rule_id": {
          "name": "decisions_rule_id",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "decisions_category": {
          "name": "decisions_category",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "decisions_category_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT')"
        },
        "decisions_automated_decision": {
          "name": "decisions_automated_decision",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" in ('fully', 'partially', 'not_automated')"
        },
        "decisions_territorial_scope": {
          "name": "decisions_territorial_scope",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"territorial_scope\" = 'worldwide'"
        },
        "decisions_review_target": {
          "name": "decisions_review_target",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"kind\" in ('review', 'correction')) = (\"decisions\".\"reviews_decision_id\" is not null) and (\"decisions\".\"kind\" = 'review') = (\"decisions\".\"appeal_id\" is not null)"
        },
        "decisions_interim": {
          "name": "decisions_interim",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" <> 'interim' or \"decisions\".\"through_seq\" = 0"
        },
        "decisions_ground_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'incompatible' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is not null"
        },
        "decisions_ground_law": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_law",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is not null"
        },
        "decisions_restricted": {
          "name": "decisions_restricted",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"outcome\" <> 'restricted' or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is not null)"
        },
        "decisions_digests": {
          "name": "decisions_digests",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')"
        },
        "decisions_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null or \"decisions\".\"ground\" is not distinct from 'illegal'"
        },
        "decisions_law_no_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_law_no_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null"
        },
        "decisions_reversal_plain": {
          "name": "decisions_reversal_plain",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" not in ('review', 'correction') or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is null and \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null and \"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null and \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null)"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },

          "name": "intakes_rule_id",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "intakes_category": {
          "name": "intakes_category",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "intakes_category_keyword": {
          "name": "intakes_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL', 'KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE', 'KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS')"
        },
        "intakes_cited_law_len": {
          "name": "intakes_cited_law_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"cited_law\") <= 300"
        },
        "intakes_explanation_len": {
          "name": "intakes_explanation_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"explanation\") <= 2000"
        },
        "intakes_has_ground": {
          "name": "intakes_has_ground",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\""
        },
        "intakes_illegal_elements": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_elements",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'user' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"bona_fide\" and (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is not null))"
        },
        "intakes_finding_legal": {
          "name": "intakes_finding_legal",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'finding' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\""
        },
        "intakes_illegal_not_tc": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_not_tc",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"category\" <> 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC'"
        },
        "intakes_csam": {
          "name": "intakes_csam",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"category\" = 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS' and \"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_contact_signed_out": {
          "name": "intakes_contact_signed_out",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out'"
        },
        "intakes_reporter_signed_in": {
          "name": "intakes_reporter_signed_in",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_in'"
        },
        "intakes_finding": {
          "name": "intakes_finding",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"finding_by\" is not null) and (\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'staff')"
        },
        "intakes_lookup": {
          "name": "intakes_lookup",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"lookup_hash\" is not null) = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out' or \"intakes\".\"csam\")"
        },
        "intakes_erased": {
          "name": "intakes_erased",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is null or (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is null and \"intakes\".\"cited_law\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_r2_finding_only": {
          "name": "intakes_r2_finding_only",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is distinct from 'R2' or \"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding'"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },
```

### Replace `apps/admin/src/screens/Home.tsx` (whole file)

```tsx
import { OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX, type AuditEntry, type StaffKey, type StaffMe, type StaffOverview, type StaffSession } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { StaffApi } from "../api";
import { APPEAL_WORDS, describeError, PROTECTION_LIFTED_WORDS } from "../messages";
import { CaseLink } from "../nav";
import { parseCaseId, type CaseId } from "../router";
import { readSignInsAtOpening } from "../signins";
import { revokeSessionWithKey } from "../step-up";
import { clockTime, dateTime, Loaded, UserText, type Loadable } from "../ui";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import type { CredentialsLike } from "../webauthn";
import { counted, LANE_NAMES, waited } from "../words";

/**
 * One of the home screen's lists of the path for child sexual abuse material: each row with its time, its staff handle
 * as text, a link to its case built from a checked id, and the console's own words for what the row is. A list holds at
 * most OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX rows, and says how many there are when there are more.
 */
function StaffList<T extends { at: string; handle: string; caseId: string }>({ title, hint, empty, list, words, onOpenCase }: { title: string; hint: string; empty: string; list: { total: number; items: T[] }; words(item: T): ReactNode; onOpenCase(id: CaseId): void }) {
  return (
    <>
      <h3>{title}</h3>
      <p className="hint">{hint}</p>
      {list.items.length === 0 ? (
        <p>{empty}</p>
      ) : (
        <ul className="reveals">
          {list.items.map((item, index) => {
            const id = parseCaseId(item.caseId);
            return (
              <li key={`${item.at} ${item.caseId} ${index}`}>
                <time dateTime={item.at}>{dateTime(item.at)}</time> <UserText>{item.handle}</UserText>{" "}
                {id ? (
                  <CaseLink id={id} onOpen={onOpenCase}>
                    the case
                  </CaseLink>
                ) : null}{" "}
                {words(item)}
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      )}
      {list.total > list.items.length ? <p>{`Showing the newest ${OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX} of ${list.total}.`}</p> : null}
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * The runbook's sentence for a count of decisions not released, in the words of the runbook's own bullet (3c design,
 * section 13, Task 12(a)). It is a constant of its own so that the test of the README's runbook can hold the two to the
 * same words: what the home screen tells staff is what the runbook tells the operator.
 */
export const RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK =
  "A count of decisions not released means the daily release keeps failing: notifiers are not told and re-examination windows do not open, so read the API log for moderation-dispatch and fix it the same day.";

/** The home screen's line when decided items wait for the daily release longer than it ever takes: the count, then the runbook's sentence for it. */
export const releaseOverdue = (n: number): string => `Decisions not released after 26 hours: ${n}. ${RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK}`;

/**
 * The runbook's sentence for a count of late erasures, in the words of the runbook's own bullet (3c design, section 13,
 * Task 12(a)), a constant of its own for the same reason as the one above.
 */
export const ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK =
  "A count of late erasures names the due rule whose step keeps failing, so evidence, an intake record or a notifier's name and address outlives its published period: read the API log for moderation-retention and for auth janitor: purge failed, and check that API_MODERATION_RETENTION was not left off after a restore (the API logs it at every start).";

/** What each count of late erasures counts, in the order the retention job's steps run; the two last are the image rows and the auth janitor's. */
export const ERASURE_OVERDUE_WORDS: Record<keyof StaffOverview["erasureOverdue"], string> = {
  drafts: "unconfirmed drafts",
  caseEvidence: "closed cases whose evidence is due",
  intakeRecords: "records of reports and notices",
  redactions: "R4 erasures",
  statements: "statements of deleted accounts",
  accessLog: "access log rows",
  images: "image rows nothing retains",
  contacts: "notifiers' contacts and confirmations",
};

/**
 * The home screen's line for what retention is late with by more than a day: each count above zero under its own words,
 * then the runbook's sentence. Null when nothing is late, and then the screen says nothing.
 */
export function erasureOverdue(counts: StaffOverview["erasureOverdue"]): string | null {
  const late = (Object.keys(ERASURE_OVERDUE_WORDS) as (keyof StaffOverview["erasureOverdue"])[]).filter((key) => counts[key] > 0).map((key) => `${ERASURE_OVERDUE_WORDS[key]}: ${counts[key]}`);
  return late.length === 0 ? null : `Erasures more than a day late: ${late.join("; ")}. ${ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK}`;
}

/**
 * What every staff member sees of the cases (3c design, section 8): the lanes with their open cases and how long the
 * oldest has waited, the appeals waiting (with those this person may review and those nobody may review now), every reveal of a source in the last 30 days with its staff handle and its
 * case, the decisions that lifted the protection of reported images, the recorded choices not to seal and the seals
 * taken while deciding that are in force, what each staff account viewed and opened today, the mails that wait or were
 * given up, and the emergency switch. Counts, times, handles and case links only.
 */
/**
 * The home screen's appeals line (3c design, section 8): how many wait, how many of them the reading person may review,
 * and how many no staff account may review now.
 */
export function appealsLine(overview: Pick<StaffOverview, "appealsWaiting" | "appealsYouMayReview" | "appealsWithoutReviewer">): string {
  const { appealsWaiting: waiting, appealsYouMayReview: yours, appealsWithoutReviewer: without } = overview;
  if (waiting === 0) return "No appeal waits.";
  const parts = [waiting === 1 ? "1 appeal waits" : `${waiting} appeals wait`, `you may review ${yours === 0 ? "none" : yours}`];
  if (without > 0) parts.push(`${without} ${without === 1 ? "has" : "have"} no possible reviewer now`);
  return `${parts.join("; ")}.`;
}

export function OverviewView({ overview, now, onOpenCase }: { overview: StaffOverview; now: number; onOpenCase(id: CaseId): void }) {
  const { reveals, mailsWaiting, mailsFailed } = overview;
  const lateErasures = erasureOverdue(overview.erasureOverdue);
  const waiting = mailsWaiting.receipts + mailsWaiting.authorMails + mailsWaiting.outcomes;
  const failed = mailsFailed.receipts + mailsFailed.authorMails + mailsFailed.outcomes;
  const mails = (m: StaffOverview["mailsWaiting"]) => `${counted(m.receipts, "receipt", "receipts")}, ${counted(m.authorMails, "statement to an author", "statements to authors")}, ${counted(m.outcomes, "outcome", "outcomes")}`;
  return (
    <>
      <h3>Cases</h3>
      <ul className="lanes">
        {overview.lanes.map((lane) => (
          <li key={lane.lane}>{`${LANE_NAMES[lane.lane]}: ${lane.open === 0 || lane.oldestAt === null ? "no open case" : `${counted(lane.open, "case", "cases")}, oldest ${waited(lane.oldestAt, now)}`}`}</li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <p>{appealsLine(overview)}</p>
      {overview.appealsWaiting > 0 ? <p className="hint">{APPEAL_WORDS.reviewerRule}</p> : null}
      <p>{overview.deferUnproven ? "The emergency switch is on: cases whose unanswered items all come from unproven sources are listed after the others of their lane." : "The emergency switch is off."}</p>
      {overview.releaseOverdue > 0 ? (
        <p role="alert" className="error">
          {releaseOverdue(overview.releaseOverdue)}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {lateErasures !== null ? (
        <p role="alert" className="error">
          {lateErasures}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {waiting > 0 ? <p className="notice">{`Mails waiting for more than an hour: ${mails(mailsWaiting)}.`}</p> : null}
      {failed > 0 ? <p className="notice">{`Mails given up in the last 30 days: ${mails(mailsFailed)}.`}</p> : null}

      <h3>Sources revealed in the last 30 days</h3>
      <p className="hint">Every staff account's. A reveal nobody expected means someone else holds a staff key: tell the operator.</p>
      {reveals.items.length === 0 ? (
        <p>No source was revealed in the last 30 days.</p>
      ) : (
        <ul className="reveals">
          {reveals.items.map((item, index) => {
            const id = parseCaseId(item.caseId);
            return (
              <li key={`${item.at} ${item.caseId} ${index}`}>
                <time dateTime={item.at}>{dateTime(item.at)}</time> <UserText>{item.handle}</UserText>{" "}
                {id ? (
                  <CaseLink id={id} onOpen={onOpenCase}>
                    the case
                  </CaseLink>
                ) : null}
              </li>
            );
          })}
        </ul>
      )}
      {reveals.total > reveals.items.length ? <p>{`Showing the newest ${OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX} of ${reveals.total}.`}</p> : null}

      <StaffList
        title="Protection of reported images lifted in the last 30 days"
        hint="Every staff account's: each lifted seal, and each admin's answer to a report or finding of child sexual abuse material without a seal. One nobody expected means someone else holds a staff key: tell the operator."
        empty="No decision lifted the protection of reported images in the last 30 days."
        list={overview.protectionLifted}
        words={(item) => PROTECTION_LIFTED_WORDS[item.kind]}
        onOpenCase={onOpenCase}
      />
      <StaffList
        title="Choices not to seal in the last 30 days"
        hint="Every staff account's: each recorded choice not to seal reported images, whose reason is on its case."
        empty="Nobody recorded a choice not to seal in the last 30 days."
        list={overview.sealsDeclined}
        words={() => "Chose not to seal"}
        onOpenCase={onOpenCase}
      />
      <StaffList
        title="Seals taken while deciding that are in force"
        hint="Which images stand sealed until an admin answers, and by whom."
        empty="No seal taken while deciding is in force."
        list={overview.interimSeals}
        words={(item) => `${counted(item.images, "image", "images")} on ${counted(item.posts, "post", "posts")}`}
        onOpenCase={onOpenCase}
      />

      <h3>Today, by staff account</h3>
      {overview.imagesToday.length === 0 && overview.findingsToday.length === 0 ? (
        <p>No image was viewed and no finding opened today.</p>
      ) : (
        <ul className="today">
          {overview.imagesToday.map((row) => (
            <li key={`images ${row.handle}`}>
              <UserText>{row.handle}</UserText>
              {`: ${counted(row.count, "image", "images")} viewed`}
            </li>
          ))}
          {overview.findingsToday.map((row) => (
            <li key={`findings ${row.handle}`}>
              <UserText>{row.handle}</UserText>
              {`: ${counted(row.count, "finding", "findings")} opened`}
            </li>
          ))}
        </ul>
      )}
    </>
  );
}

/**
 * The home screen (3a design, section 9; 3c design, section 8): who is signed in and with which role, the session's
 * absolute end, the cases' overview, every staff account's sign-ins of the last 7 days, the person's own staff sessions
 * with "Sign out that session" confirmed by the key, and the person's keys. Keys are added and revoked only with the
 * command line, so no button here touches them.
 */
export interface HomeViewProps {
  me: StaffMe;
  overview: Loadable<StaffOverview>;
  /** The time the overview's waiting times are counted to. */
  now: number;
  onOpenCase(id: CaseId): void;
  signIns: Loadable<AuditEntry[]>;
  sessions: Loadable<StaffSession[]>;
  keys: Loadable<StaffKey[]>;
  /** The handle of the session whose revocation is under way. */
  revoking: string | null;
  notice: string | null;
  error: string | null;
  onRevoke(handle: string): void;
}

export function HomeView({ me, overview, now, onOpenCase, signIns, sessions, keys, revoking, notice, error, onRevoke }: HomeViewProps) {
  return (
    <section aria-labelledby="home-title">
      <h2 id="home-title">Home</h2>
      <p>
        Signed in as <UserText>{me.handle}</UserText>, {me.role}.
      </p>
      <p>{`Signed in until ${clockTime(me.absoluteExpiresAt)}.`}</p>
      {notice ? (
        <p role="status" className="notice">
          {notice}
        </p>
      ) : null}
      {error ? (
        <p role="alert" className="error">
          {error}
        </p>
      ) : null}

      <Loaded value={overview} render={(value) => <OverviewView overview={value} now={now} onOpenCase={onOpenCase} />} />

      <h3>Staff sign-ins in the last 7 days</h3>
      <p className="hint">Every staff account's, newest first. A sign-in nobody recognises means someone else holds a staff key: tell the operator.</p>
      <Loaded
        value={signIns}
        render={(list) =>
          list.length === 0 ? (
            <p>No staff sign-ins in the last 7 days.</p>
          ) : (
            <ul className="signins">
              {list.map((entry) => (
                <li key={entry.seq}>
                  <time dateTime={entry.createdAt}>{dateTime(entry.createdAt)}</time> <UserText>{entry.actorHandle ?? "no handle"}</UserText>
                </li>
              ))}
            </ul>
          )
        }
      />

      <h3>Your staff sessions</h3>
      <p className="hint">Signing out another session asks your staff key to confirm it.</p>
      <Loaded
        value={sessions}
        render={(list) => (
          <table>
            <caption className="visually-hidden">Your staff sessions</caption>
            <thead>
              <tr>
                <th scope="col">Browser</th>
                <th scope="col">Started</th>
                <th scope="col">Last used</th>
                <th scope="col">
                  <span className="visually-hidden">Sign out</span>
                </th>
              </tr>
            </thead>
            <tbody>
              {list.map((session) => (
                <tr key={session.handle}>
                  <td>
                    <UserText>{session.browser}</UserText>
                  </td>
                  <td>{dateTime(session.createdAt)}</td>
                  <td>{dateTime(session.lastUsedAt)}</td>
                  <td>
                    {session.current ? (
                      "This session"
                    ) : (
                      <button type="button" onClick={() => onRevoke(session.handle)} disabled={revoking !== null} aria-busy={revoking === session.handle}>
                        Sign out that session
                      </button>
                    )}
                  </td>
                </tr>
              ))}
            </tbody>
          </table>
        )}
      />

      <h3>Your staff keys</h3>
      <p className="hint">The operator adds and revokes staff keys with the staff command line.</p>
      <Loaded
        value={keys}
        render={(list) => (
          <ul className="keys">
            {list.map((key) => (
              <li key={key.id}>
                <UserText>{key.name}</UserText>
                {`: added ${dateTime(key.createdAt)}, ${key.lastUsedAt === null ? "never used" : `last used ${dateTime(key.lastUsedAt)}`}`}
              </li>
            ))}
          </ul>
        )}
      />
    </section>
  );
}

/** Runs one read and hands its outcome to `set`, unless the screen has gone meanwhile. */
function load<T>(alive: { current: boolean }, set: (value: Loadable<T>) => void, read: () => Promise<T>): void {
  read().then(
    (value) => alive.current && set({ state: "ready", value }),
    (err: unknown) => alive.current && set({ state: "failed", message: describeError(err) }),
  );
}

/** The person's staff sessions, marked: the screen reads them when it opens and after a revocation the person asked for. */
function readSessions(api: StaffApi, alive: { current: boolean }, set: (value: Loadable<StaffSession[]>) => void): void {
  load(alive, set, async () => (await api.sessions({ activity: true })).sessions);
}

/** Where the screen's lists go as each read finishes. */
export interface HomeLists {
  overview(value: Loadable<StaffOverview>): void;
  signIns(value: Loadable<AuditEntry[]>): void;
  sessions(value: Loadable<StaffSession[]>): void;
  keys(value: Loadable<StaffKey[]>): void;
}

/**
 * What the screen reads when it opens, every read marked, since opening the screen is its person's action. It takes no
 * session: the sign-ins' 7 days are counted from a /me read now (readSignInsAtOpening), never from the session the page
 * holds, which can be hours old.
 */
export function openHome(api: StaffApi, alive: { current: boolean }, set: HomeLists): void {
  load(alive, set.signIns, () => readSignInsAtOpening(api));
  load(alive, set.overview, () => api.overview({ activity: true }));
  readSessions(api, alive, set.sessions);
  load(alive, set.keys, async () => (await api.keys({ activity: true })).keys);
}

export function Home({ me, api, credentials, onOpenCase }: { me: StaffMe; api: StaffApi; credentials: CredentialsLike; onOpenCase(id: CaseId): void }) {
  const [overview, setOverview] = useState<Loadable<StaffOverview>>({ state: "loading" });
  const [now, setNow] = useState(() => Date.now());
  const [signIns, setSignIns] = useState<Loadable<AuditEntry[]>>({ state: "loading" });
  const [sessions, setSessions] = useState<Loadable<StaffSession[]>>({ state: "loading" });
  const [keys, setKeys] = useState<Loadable<StaffKey[]>>({ state: "loading" });
  const [revoking, setRevoking] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [notice, setNotice] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null);
  const alive = useRef(true);

  useEffect(() => {
    alive.current = true;
    openHome(api, alive, {
      overview: (value) => {
        setNow(Date.now());
        setOverview(value);
      },
      signIns: setSignIns,
      sessions: setSessions,
      keys: setKeys,
    });
    return () => {
      alive.current = false;
    };
    // Read once per opening of the screen, never again when the idle timer's reads change `me`; the API client never
    // changes while the page lives.
  }, [api]);

  const revoke = async (handle: string) => {
    setRevoking(handle);
    setNotice(null);
    setError(null);
    try {
      const outcome = await revokeSessionWithKey({ api, credentials }, handle);
      if (!alive.current) return;
      setNotice(outcome === "revoked" ? "That session is signed out." : "That session had already ended.");
      readSessions(api, alive, setSessions);
    } catch (err) {
      if (alive.current) setError(describeError(err));
    } finally {
      if (alive.current) setRevoking(null);
    }
  };

  return (
    <HomeView me={me} overview={overview} now={now} onOpenCase={onOpenCase} signIns={signIns} sessions={sessions} keys={keys} revoking={revoking} notice={notice} error={error} onRevoke={(handle) => void revoke(handle)} />
  );
}
```

```ts
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { AuthForAccount } from "../auth";
import type { MediaForAccount } from "../media";
import type { ModerationForAccount } from "../moderation";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { SocialForAccount } from "../social";

/** The codes this module raises itself; the modules it calls raise their own, which the app's error handler also renders. */
export type AccountErrorKind = "not_found" | "invalid_request" | "rate_limited" | "service_unavailable";
export type AccountErrorStatus = 400 | 404 | 429 | 503;

const MESSAGES: Record<AccountErrorKind, string> = {
  not_found: "Not found.",
  invalid_request: "Some details are missing or invalid.",
  rate_limited: "Too many requests. Wait a moment and try again.",
  service_unavailable: "That could not be done right now. Try again in a moment.",
};

/** An expected, user-facing failure. The HTTP layer turns it into an ErrorEnvelope with this code and status. */
export class AccountError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: AccountErrorKind,
    readonly status: AccountErrorStatus,
    message: string = MESSAGES[code],
    /** Set for rate_limited and service_unavailable so the response can carry Retry-After. */
    readonly retryAfterSeconds?: number,
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "AccountError";
  }
}

export function accountErrorMessage(code: AccountErrorKind): string {
  return MESSAGES[code];
}

/**
 * The account module owns no table: it sequences the other three modules through the interfaces their
 * index files export (1b design, section 5). The limit store is the one every per-account limit uses.
 */
export interface AccountDeps {
  auth: AuthForAccount;
  social: SocialForAccount;
  media: MediaForAccount;
  /**
   * The purge's forgetting of a deleted account's reports, in the moderation module's tables (3c design, section 7.10).
   * The server always hands it over; a test of the other steps may leave it out, and the purge then skips that step.
   */
  moderation?: ModerationForAccount;
  limits: RateLimitStore;
  log: Logger;
  now: () => Date;
}
```

### Replace `apps/api/src/account/flows/deletion.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import type { DeleteConfirmRequest, DeleteStartResponse } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { RequestContext, Session } from "../../auth";
import type { AccountDeps } from "../context";

/** The code goes to the account's own address; that is the auth module's alone (1b design, section 7.6). */
export function startDeletion(deps: AccountDeps, session: Session, ctx: RequestContext): Promise<DeleteStartResponse> {
  return deps.auth.startDeletion(session, ctx);
}

/**
 * Steps 2 to 4 of section 7.6, for an account the auth module has marked deleted: the social purge,
 * with the image rows detached and their files asked for inside its transaction; then the forgetting
 * of the reports the account sent (3c design, section 7.10: the database acts only on an account whose
 * auth row is marked deleted, which the take-down did before any step here); then the auth row's
 * anonymisation. The files are asked for before the commit, not after it: were the process to stop
 * between a commit and the request, a rerun would find no rows left, mark the account purged and
 * leave the files to the sweeper's reconcile pass, which refuses to act on many orphans at once. A
 * request is one empty file per id, so a rerun after a failed commit, which finds the same rows again,
 * asks again for the same ids and changes nothing; the files it asked for belong to an account that is
 * being deleted either way. Every step changes only what is still there, so the purge can run again
 * after a failure, from the request or from the job, and finish what an earlier run left.
 */
export async function purge(deps: AccountDeps, userId: string): Promise<void> {
  await deps.social.purgeProfile(userId, deps.now(), async (tx) => {
    await deps.media.requestDeletion(await deps.media.purgeOwner(tx, userId));
  });
  // After the profile is marked deleted and before the account counts as purged: a failure here leaves the purge pending,
  // and its rerun, like every step's, changes nothing that is already done.
  await deps.moderation?.forgetAccount(userId);
  await deps.auth.finishPurge(userId);
}

/**
 * The auth module checks the handle and the code and takes the account down (step 1); from there the
 * account is gone whatever happens next. The purge runs here so the owner's request answers only once
 * their posts and images are gone (seconds, for a large account). Should it fail, the failure is logged
 * and the request still succeeds: the purge job finishes any deletion left half done within five minutes.
 */
export async function confirmDeletion(deps: AccountDeps, session: Session, input: DeleteConfirmRequest): Promise<void> {
  await deps.auth.confirmDeletion(session, input);
  try {
    await purge(deps, session.userId);
  } catch (err) {
    deps.log.error({ err, userId: session.userId }, "account deletion: the purge failed after the confirmation; the purge job will finish it");
  }
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The only file outside `src/account/` may import. Everything else in the module is private and the
 * architecture test fails the build if another file reaches into it.
 */
import type { MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
import type { Logger } from "pino";
import type { AuthForAccount } from "../auth";
import type { AppEnv } from "../env";
import type { JobLock } from "../lib/jobs";
import type { MediaForAccount } from "../media";
import type { ModerationForAccount } from "../moderation";
import type { RateLimitStore } from "../middleware/rate-limit";
import type { SocialForAccount } from "../social";
import type { AccountDeps } from "./context";
import { createPurgeJob } from "./purge";
import { accountRoutes } from "./routes";

export { AccountError } from "./context";
export type { AccountDeps } from "./context";

export interface CreateAccountOptions {
  /** The other modules' interfaces for this one, as their index files hand them out: auth.forAccount, social.forAccount, media.forAccount. */
  auth: AuthForAccount;
  social: SocialForAccount;
  media: MediaForAccount;
  /** The moderation module's interface for this one: moderation.forAccount. Without it the purge forgets no report's sender. */
  moderation?: ModerationForAccount;
  /** The auth module's requireSession: an onboarded account with CSRF and Origin checked. */
  requireSession: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's requireFreshAuth: a credential proven in the last five minutes, which the export needs. */
  requireFreshAuth: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The auth module's requireStrongFreshAuth: level 2 on an account with TOTP, which starting and confirming a deletion need (1c design, section 10). */
  requireStrongFreshAuth: MiddlewareHandler<AppEnv>;
  /** The daily export limit shares the store the per-IP middleware uses. */
  rateLimitStore: RateLimitStore;
  logger: Logger;
  now?: () => Date;
}

export function createAccount(options: CreateAccountOptions) {
  const deps: AccountDeps = {
    auth: options.auth,
    social: options.social,
    media: options.media,
    moderation: options.moderation,
    limits: options.rateLimitStore,
    log: options.logger,
    now: options.now ?? (() => new Date()),
  };
  return {
    deps,
    routes: accountRoutes(deps, options.requireSession, options.requireFreshAuth, options.requireStrongFreshAuth),
    /** Starts the purge job (deletions left half done, every five minutes under the shared lock) and returns the function that stops it. */
    startPurge: (lock: JobLock) => createPurgeJob(deps, lock).start(),
  };
}

export type Account = ReturnType<typeof createAccount>;
```
